Perhaps the film's greatest strength is that it does a great job of developing a display of what I've always seen as a looming truth: it's not the industry itself that destroys people who get involved, it's what the individual seeks from the industry. I've always thought that if someone gets into porn for the sole purpose of fame and/or money, with no passion for the actual sex acts, that is precisely how one may find themselves in a vapid black hole of loneliness or unhealthy practices. Overly competitive people have always rubbed me wrong, and this movie focuses precisely on how detrimental that can be. I'll never understand the need to be "the best" - just love what you do!This was a somewhat surreal viewing experience for me considering I "know" 80% of the cast, as well as in about half of the locations that the film took place in - that's a first with a mainstream film. I enjoyed watching all these acquaintances getting their chance to flex their acting chops in a somewhat different realm. Lead actress Sofia Kappel (one of the only cast members who's not actually in the porn industry) absolutely stole the show, delivering a brave, well-rounded, and pretty endearing performance, which gives the movie a lot of life and value it might not otherwise have. Ex-pornstar Zelda Morrison did a fantastic job building a realistic character throughout the film, as did fellow XXX talent Chris Cock. And, Evelyn Claire, who has always reminded me of young Jennifer Connelly, was the PERFECT casting choice for her very crucial role - she serves absolute FACE every single time she's on screen - she's stone cold.While I felt that the movie didn't have a lot of dynamic to it's pacing, and kind of lacked some necessary tension, I still think it's a very accomplished showcase of what performing in the industry is like for those curious to know. It's shot well and I enjoyed the direction of the music used. It is a VERY graphic film, hence the NOT RATED rating, so of course it's not for everyone! Plentiful erect penises and interpreted sex acts and cum! Not sure i'd ever watch it again, but, it stands out!

title: What's your pleasure?
author: Pjtaylor-96-138044
body: 'Pleasure (2021)' isn't exactly an enjoyable experience, and the irony of its title doesn't seem lost on writer-director Ninja Thyberg. This frank and unapologetic exploration of the Los Angeles porn industry almost feels like an exposé at times, with its naturalistic presentation granting it a fly-on-the-wall feel which makes its more shocking moments all the more upsetting. Indeed, there are a few scenes which are incredibly difficult to watch. The most notable of these is the filming of a rough and degrading three-way scene which our protagonist continues to consent to only because she has no other option - which, of course, means she doesn't consent at all. It stands in stark contrast to a similar scene shown just minutes earlier, the shooting of which has its star surrounded by people who make sure she's comfortable and genuinely feel as though they're concerned for her safety (it's no accident that a lot of these people are women). The picture constantly presents this push-pull between how the porn industry ought to work and how it actually does, remaining relatively neutral to the concept but condemning its execution. Having said that, the overwhelming feeling that this picture provokes is undeniably icky. If porn is something you're into, I can see this actually putting you off. Whether or not that is its intention is unclear, especially considering that the flick does go out of its way to include both the good and the bad parts of its protagonist's journey. Perhaps its goal is to be as realistic as possible, not necessarily impartial but not forceful in its implied assertions. I suppose this is how it manages to be both empathetic and non-judgemental towards the women who seek a career in porn and unsympathetic towards the men who take advantage of them. Though the feature isn't especially entertaining in the traditional sense (it certainly isn't fun), it's a consistently challenging and compelling affair that manages to be explicit enough to feel as though it's doing its taboo subject justice (and to be genuinely shocking at times) but not so explicit as to feel as though it's overly gratuitous or insensitive. Sofia Kappel delivers a bold, bracing debut performance (apparently, auditioning for the film was a way to push her out of her comfort zone) and the rest of its cast - which is mostly comprised of current or former porn performers, producers and directors - is surprisingly good, too. The flick doesn't feel exploitative at all, taking a fairly feminist approach to its material and always feeling like it has something to say. Everything we see is necessary in telling this tale, which is rare even for something that isn't dealing with a potentially tricky topic. It's funny how nobody blinks an eye when seeing someone's head get blown off in a movie, but almost everyone feels at least a little uncomfortable when someone takes their clothes off and starts having sex. This piece almost strives to make you uncomfortable because it wants you to face the realities of a pretty shady business. The interesting thing about it, though, is that it isn't the sex itself that gets under your skin. Sexual violence is presented as truly disgusting and upsetting, as it should be, but it's also presented as insidious and pervasive. It isn't something that just happens, it's something that's enabled and justified by those with the power to do so. It works its way into every industry one way or another, so it's naturally present in an industry that concerns itself almost solely with sex. The thing is, though, it shouldn't be. Sex work is work and everyone deserves to be and feel safe in their workplace. Tangent aside, this is a strong movie that's as engaging as it is off-putting. If you can handle it, it's worth a watch.

title: Incredibly nuanced for such a heavy subject matter
author: isaacsundaralingam
body: It's pretty much true that everytime there's a mainstream movie about the adult industry, it always focuses on the extremes on one end; where there tends to be a very anti-porn industry undertone that guides these movies.So when you're making a movie about the industry with many actual performers showing up as themselves, there was the risk of it being extreme on the pro-industry end. But to my pleasant surprise, the movie composed itself with a lot of nuance on both ends of the argument to share its story without a strong bias on either side; something I very much appreciate. Pleasure is a very decent movie, but with very little originality in my opinion. Yes, I liked its tone overall, but the story plays out exactly the way you'd think it would by the first 15 minutes. It certainly wasn't boring, but it never captivated as much as it had the potential to, and that's something I wish this movie could have done different.Overall however, it was a decent watch, but more importantly, it was made with the right frame of mind... and that's what truly stood out to me.

title: Realistic portrayal of the US porn industry
author: cotta002-318-865119
body: A girl from Sweden decides she wants to make it in the LA porn scene and become a star.The movie starts with her landing in LAX airport and subsequently being housed in a rental for girls in the porn industry (a common practice).The movie holds no punches as it shows the way an adult performer becomes a commodity and how time is money.A few sympathetic characters however most are shallow and some are cruel.This movie does not hold back and is pretty much accurate in how the porn business is.She has to decide whether to roll with it or to take a stand on principles, oh how a day can change one's mind.Some cameos by real porn stars and crew, actors were great especially the lead.Definitely one to see.

title: Everything you always wanted to know about porn industries but were afraid to ask...!
author: shahrad
body: Perhaps the most authentic approach to the genre. A full yet brief closure to legal porn industries. Not a great movie in terms of cinematic values but an explicit look to this mesmerizing world, containing lots of graphic sexual moments, intelligently put for the sake of story.A unique film you don't get to see all the time.

title: Euro arthouse meets LA porn scene
author: gregorik
body: Contrary to what a number of reviewers enthuse about this film, there is nothing "revolutionary" about it as far as edgy European filmmakers are concerned. In fact, the likes of Paul Verhoeven, Gaspard Noe and Ulrich Seidl did much of the heavy lifting several years before, in terms of explicit and frank cinema-verite material.That said, this is a compelling, carefully researched slice-of-life movie with a central performance for the ages, and it's coming from perfect newcomer Sofia Kappel. With a less game actress, this could have been just another "Showgirls".The director's insistence on sticking to crushing realism means that there's a complete lack of Hollywood moments, twists and turns, and no artificial tension -- which would admittedly make the whole affair an easier watch. It's never boring, but there's a distinct documentarist feel to everything, which does kill any budding drama.Make no mistake, this is a European art movie, transplanted to the LA p*rn scene.

title: Ambition, abjection, compromise and insight
author: jimcheva
body: I've seen at least one doc on porn life and more than one film that shows it, so there wasn't much here that would shock me. I think the most striking thing about the film is how much of what we see could be true across the film industry - women cheapening themselves more or less willingly in hopes of getting ahead, a progressive surrender of idealism, some unpleasant surprises, decidng to work past them until one or does not decide the price is worth paying to get where you want to be. Much of what we see is the maturation or hardening - depending on your point of view - of someone coming to terms with the requirements of a predatory world (and porn is far from the only such world in LA) while - possibly less realistically - questioning the price of her own ambition. Apparently many of the performers here are actual porn performers, which mainly shows in their ease in certain scenes. But there is a lot of good emotional life in their work as well. Anyone who watches this mainly for the sex is likely to be disappointed - there are non-porn related films with more overt sexual scenes - and some might find it simply hard to watch at times. But it's a real story with a real progress and real relationships that happens to be set in the world of porn.

title: A daring and valid inside look
author: fredrikgunerius
body: A daring and valid inside look into the modern porn business, with only slight hints of affectation and message by Swedish filmmaker Ninja Thyberg, based on her own award-winning 2013 short. Sofia Kappel plays the 19-year-old Swedish girl Linnéa who travels to Los Angeles determined to become a porn star, and Pleasure tells the story of how she loses her last drops of naïvete and becomes a full-blown cynic, without simplifying her psychological transformation or the business in general. There are a handful of really powerful segments in here, not least the depiction of Bella Cherry's first BDSM scene, and the film is at its best when Thyberg treats the material without prejudice or emotion, letting the audience make its own conclusions. Kappel gives a powerful and nuanced lead performance in what was her debut movie. Several of her co-stars are real-life porn actors.

title: Just an HONEST OBJECTIVE REVIEW

body: Okay so "Pleasure" delves into what it is like to be a porn star. It comes equipped with all of the debauchery you would expect to portray this sometimes sordid craft. Even to the difficulties that male porn stars experience with 'being prepared and ready to go'Boogie Nights was the only other film to really memorialize the porn industry and obviously it was fantastic. title: The pleasure and the pain of porn
author: russelldresearch
body: I'm guessing that this movie got low ratings from many men because it wasn't the straightforward pornographic movie they were expecting. Though I'm sure some still managed to get sexual relief from watching this movie, most would have been turned off by this hard, gruesome look at the porn industry through the eyes of one woman. And that's because that is the intention of the movie: to get the viewer to see the true nature of the hidden process that leads to their sexual self-pleasuring product. Sadistic and aggressive porn is the most worrying, not least because it leads some men to believe such sex is the norm rather than a minority interest. Increasingly, porn degrades and devalues sexual love and pleasure - it's almost the opposite of eroticism. Comparing porn to eroticism is like comparing fast food to a 5-star gourmet meal.Anyone who is into porn but feels a growing unease about what they see should watch this movie and examine their own attitudes to visual depictions of sexual activity, to women, and to their own sexuality. Though porn can now be obtained free on the internet, it isn't free - it has a cost, and that cost is the potential corruption of your own sexual feelings and your attitudes to sex; as well as the exploitation of many women who are coerced and forced into making porn movies.The lead actress Sofia Kappel gives a stunning performance as a young girl trying to make it in the US porn industry, and the movie is well directed, skilfully edited, and has impressive production values. But if it makes you feel as much disgust and disdain as I did, this is a movie you will want to watch only once, unless you are addicted to porn - one of the few pleasures which is more habit forming than heroin, and as destructive as alcohol and tobacco.

The plot is simple and straightforward: Bella Cherry wants to be the next big thing in the industry, but she will soon discover that fame has a price. The problem is that no one forced them to choose this line of work. If you really want to be part of this world, you should inform yourself a bit better on what you are getting into. These ain't the 80's anymore, when people did not know what was happening behind the scenes.

title: Heavy on atmosphere and sexual subversion, yet unhappily light in insight
author: YellowManReanimated
body: Pleasure is the story of 19-year-old Swede Bella Cherry (Sofia Kappel) and her attempts to establish herself in the LA porn scene. She claims that she wants to become the world's next big porn star; however, achieving this goal will prove to be anything other than simple. Along her journey, she meets a variety of performers, agents and directors, all of whom are at different levels in the porn pyramid. If she wants to get to the top, she will have to become a fearless, dedicated performer, and go beyond emotional and physical boundaries that she could only previously have imagined attempting to cross. She quickly learns that the porn world is an intense, sometimes brutal, sometimes insane place to be, and it is not certain that Bella Cherry has what is takes to survive.The debut feature effort of both director Ninja Thyberg and actress Sofia Kappel, Pleasure is a film which is extremely comfortable with making its audience squirm. This starts from one of the film's first scenes, which has an extreme close-up of Bella's most intimate region while she shaves herself in preparation for her first shoot. There is a slight scratch just above the perineal area which has previously been bleeding. Such details immediately remove the arousal that a young, naked woman in another context might elicit. They show her physical vulnerability, thus, her humanity. From there, we must bear witness to Bella being directed in a sex scene with a man who is more than twice her age. She is instructed as to how to move, where to look and what to say as she gets to work on fellating and copulating her way through her first scene. Shots of erect penises and ejaculation are filmed in a way that is more akin to something from a horror film than a sex scene. Thyberg has a way of visually emphasising the coldness and detachment that engaging in such work involves. The way the male's erection engorges the camera in extreme close-up is reminiscent of one of Ridley Scott's aliens emerging into shot on U. S. S Sulaco. Bella then films herself at the end of the scene on her smartphone with her face covered in ejaculate, a substance that doesn't look too dissimilar to that which infamously burst from John Hurt's character from the same film. The scene is a brilliant evocation of naked objectification. Sex for money is literally shown as invasive, intrusive, borderline horrific and fundamentally unarousing.This is one of the great strengths of Thyberg's film; it completely subverts the purpose of pornography. There is very little that is titilating about Pleasure, a film title that is very much a misnomer. There are also insights into the off-camera realities of porn as the audience is exposed to the insidious psychological manipulation which takes place. Whenever Bella gets uncomfortable and does not wish to continue with a scene, the directors often know the right words to use and the right approaches to take in order to get her to do their bidding. They'll be encouraging, sensitive and supportive when necessary and they'll be threatening, hostile and borderline forceful when it suits. However, it would be wrong to see these people as the enemy. What lies behind all of the film's events, no matter how uncomfortable and dark they become, is the fact that Bella is there to experience them of her own volition. In fact, she has travelled halfway across the world to have these experiences. And so that takes us to a pretty salient question: why?This is where the film struggles. The motivations for Bella's desire to be part of a world which she clearly finds alienating and intimidating are never made clear. This is despite Kappel giving a flawless performance in the central role. She exudes both fearlessness and extreme vulnerability; cold detachment and youthful naivety; single-minded ambition and profound ambivalence. There is so much range to Kappel's performance but the character is not written in such a way as to find any central motivation. Porn is a world of extremes and only extreme personalities belong there. Bella doesn't seem to be all that interested in sex, in fact the film never depicts her having sex off camera. There is no evidence of any events from her past influencing her decision either. Quite the opposite, the cliché of all pornstars being abused as children is very quickly mocked and dismissed in the early scenes of the film. So why is she there? Is she just a product of an extreme generation that is so obsessed with Warhol's predicted fifteen-minutes of fame that she'll take whatever route best available to get her there? This is never made clear. And the fact that the film is so tightly focused on her character (she is in literally every scene) means that it is hard to find any reason to extrapolate from her character to her generation as a whole. It is worth noting that the only scene we get which reveals anything of Bella's life back in Sweden only confuses matters even more. The background motivations for her actions just don't seem to be present.What we have, then, is a twisted, subversive film experience in which a young, pretty naive woman is thrust into an environment of humiliation, degradation and brutality. We are shown sex scenes which are not arousing. We are shown glamour which is utterly unappealing. We are shown a character who is trying to establish herself in a world that is constantly in flux. The art direction is astounding and the soundtrack is atmospheric and unsettling, while the overall tone of the film is unflinchingly menacing. Yet, despite some interesting reveals as to attitudes and approaches which exist behind the camera, and despite the heavy on-camera involvement of actors and directors directly from the porn industry, what we do not get is a genuine insight into the mindset of a porn star. Bella is quite simply an abstraction of a real-life porn performer, she's not the real deal. As interesting and as darkly engaging as this film is, less atmosphere and more psychological revelation could have led to a genuinely vital document. Most of us will have been exposed to, or exposed ourselves to, porn at some point in our lives. It is now virtually ubiquitous. But how many of us truly understand what the porn industry is, or what motivates its most recognised performers? I'm not sure I do, and I don't really feel much the wiser for having watched this film.

title: A dive into the adult film industry
author: meinwonderland
body: A dive into the adult film industry where the alluring opportunities and unglamorous aspects of its harsh reality converge to make or break dreams of aspiring actors.Ninja Thyberg's Pleasure is interested in examining themes of ambition as well as friendship. Linnéa, aka Bella Cherry, played by Sofia Kappel, is a young Swedish aspiring actress in Los Angeles who will find in the adult film industry not only a medium to self-realization, but also difficulties that will challenge her rise, if she has what it takes to succeed, as well as to make her question if that career is the right one for her. By framing universal themes in this workplace, Ninja Thyberg allows us to delve into an industry known by few. An industry that, viewed from the inside, lacks what might be at first sight supposed as abounding, eroticism. There is always a very professional atmosphere in the workplace where those scenes are made where consent forms are signed and recorded, and assistants are always trying to make of the set an amiable environment for the people involved. There is an artificiality bathing the sets, often in mansions with minimalism style where a detachment to any identity or personal item is enforced. Pleasure doesn't shy away from graphicness, there are a lot of scenes where sexual content is depicted as anything but pleasurable. Scenes that capture how gruesome, sometimes even disturbing, this industry can be. There is a constant dehumanization in the set, the extent of some of the demands actors are asked to perform can be close to nauseating, making some scenes hard to watch.Unlike most of the stories portraying sex work, Pleasure doesn't judge Bella's choices. Her reasons are not based on a psychologically troubled past or trauma, but on her preferences and ambition alone. An ambition that fuels her motivation to achieve her goals by climbing the ladder to success. The movie clearly defines hierarchy in the framework of the industry. On one side we have Ava (Evelyn Claire), the beautiful new Spiegler Girl, and on the other Joy (Revika Anne Reustle), Bella's roommate who was called "trailer trash" by another actor. A defined hierarchy that helps as a blue map for Bella to follow. One of the things the movie achieves is communicating Bella's emotions without relying on dialogue alone, and by doing so, not underestimating the medium. In the same way many scenes are difficult to watch due to their explicitness, there are others that feel liberating not by themselves, but by what came before. Because, in the narrative of the movie, they symbolize much more than the physical acts they portray, they are symbols of atonements.

title: Too long and too slow.
author: Top_Dawg_Critic
body: This story is about Bella's journey, but it felt more like a walk around the block. This film suffered many rookie filmmaking mistakes, the biggest being its failure to effectively deliver its message effectively about its bold subject matter. It had a lot of style, but very little substance. In the film's 109 min runtime, there are far too many long and dragged out scenes, and with the slow pacing, the film just dragged on. This may have worked better as a short film, or needed stronger filmmakers to tune up the directing and writing. The story lacked character depth, and wasted time with roommate dynamics instead of focusing more on the industry dynamics. There certainly were touches and flashes on the narrative's message, but they were too narrow, hollow and simplistic. It's well shot with decent cinematography with an adequate score and performances, but sadly, it ended up being limp.

title: Undecided
author: slzoras
body: The movie has great performances, and you can tell there's a lot of attention to details and to make everything seem as realistic as possible. The main issue of this movie is the fact that the movie tries to be two things at the same time: a realistic, ambiguous and un-judgemental look at the porn industry, with its highs and lows, and also a complex character study about a normal girl internalizing the trauma of "being used" for success. The somber camera work, the details of the "technicalities" of porn, the hyper realistic dialogue, it all would suggest that the movie wants you to digest this strange experience as a whole, but at the same time there's also a repeating (and kind of annoying) angelic choir theme contrasted with a trap-rap song, to highlight the un-sacred and perverted nature of all of this, you also have some scenes with overt representation of trauma and violence, you have a soundtrack and a heavy focus on a single character. So the issue is that I don't know what to think. It's a mix between a Black Swan type story set in porn and a documentaristic look on a very complex reality. It gives you lots of emotionality and too few characters to be really an impartial look, and it's way too understated and ambiguous to be an intensely emotional character study. What is it?I commend the effort, but I feel like this movie half-does a lot and fully commits to nothing, and that probably ensures me I won't really remember much about it.

body: Not for the faint of heart, this movie has it all. Pleasure mostly does it right. But tends to falter in certain areas namely purpose and character. You really get no much more than a short glimpse. The lack of backstory contributes to the lesser investment throughout the movie. Generally though I think it works well as a educator, not a wake-up call perse, but a reminder of what the industry is about and how it works, even though it is always changing.Directing was solid, some scenes worked better than others, personally the angelic soundtrack felt a bit empty, only to contrast the act's as some sort of sin? Either way it didn't sit right with me, especially as the theme is only found in the soundtrack and nowhere else. In terms of what this movie is trying to be it seems like it wanted to be a character study but took too much time showcasing different film sets and methods. I think as a movie it would have had more impact with more character depth and time spent with Bella. Like the bdsm and the rough scene are both kind of the same, the rough scene works for the movie later but not the bdsm so it felt like filler afterwards.Acting is fantastic by pretty much everyone involved, cannot be understated how a tough a role lik this must be and to do it convincingly. Reading that this is Sofia Kappel's first role is insane. In a way she mirrors her character in the film (dd scene). The little character relationship between Bella and Joy was nice and felt genuine.It's mostly drama, maybe they tried some comedy with the stereotypical directors and such but that never landed for me, I never laughed once during the movie.The male dominated world is definitely strongly represented in this movie but it's not overbearing. Thankfully it doesn't go ''men bad'' but instead has a few moments where the male performers are also shown as humans and have just a tough of a job sometimes.Bella's character arc felt somewhat fast but it's understandable, but we still don't fully get it, we are as confused as she is and the finale shows that again. You could reduce it to a more simple matter but without backstory we don't truly know her motivation, we can only guess behind the lies she tells.Generally interesting but not as impactful as I'd hoped.

title: From obedience to becoming a tormenter
author: alex_with_a_P
body:
A rough movie to watch in certain parts. It's an important look into the porn industry from the point of view of a up-and-coming actress. It has a lot of empathy in terms that we see the movie from her eyes in more ways than you would like. It can be deeply disturbing for some viewers, but I also think it should. I think it's still successful in it's main goal is to immerse yourself in this seedy world and see what women have to go through with your own eyes..
There's a lot of psychology at play. Mirrors play a big part in this movie, and certain scenes mirror other deeper relationships like the phone call to her Mom, and the obedience the industry demands.Where the movie shines is that it's very good at telling the story visually. Especially the last ten minutes are impressive when our protagonist goes into the deepest abyss and becomes what the industry expects her to be. The shot with the two women in the limousine, motionless like dolls is great and tells so many things without any dialogue.Uncomfortable, sometimes meandering? Yes, but it's still an interesting insight on the underbelly of the pleasure industry.

title: The only film where you'll find a cat, dog, capybara, lemur, and bird teaming up.
author: michellekiara
body: Before last year, I wasn't particularly drawn to films without dialogue, as I found them somewhat dull and pretentious. This perception shifted dramatically after I encountered "Robot Dreams" at the Melbourne Film Festival last year, which quickly became my number one favorite film of all time. This experience opened my eyes to the potential depth and intrigue of dialogue-free storytelling."Flow" further solidified my appreciation for this style. This film tells the story of a cat whose life is upended by a massive flood, leading to an unexpected and touching alliance with a diverse group of animals: a capybara, a bird, a lemur, and a dog. The premise of the film is utterly unique, unlike anything I've seen before, and it brings a fresh, whimsical twist to the genre.What really stood out to me was the meticulous attention to detail in depicting each animal's behavior and the interactions among them. The film's creators clearly conducted extensive research to ensure the authenticity of each species' characteristics, which translated into animations that were not only accurate but incredibly engaging. Each character was crafted with distinct personality traits and quirks, making them memorable and endearing.

title: My kind of a story

title: Catsaway
author: MogwaiMovieReviews
body: Impressive independent animation from Latvia, wordlessly telling the story of a bunch of animals working together to help each other survive after a cataclysmic flood.The movement of the animals and depiction of the natural world is stunning and incredibly lifelike, although the animals look strangely blocky and unfinished up close, as if they ran out of funding to finish off adding details such as fur.The selfless behaviour of some of the animals often seems too far-fetched to buy into, and seeing them competently steer a boat to harbour seems similarly hard-to-swallow. On top of that, the story seems a little too vague and unmoored from a followable narrative, meaning some of the environments they pass through look like little more than video game levels, dreamt up to look nice but not communicating anything meaningful about the wider world in which they are situated.For all this, the immersive details and sheer FLOW of the film just about makes up for these shortcomings and carries one along in its wake, engrossed and entertained, to the end. Well worth a watch.

title: Masterpiece
author: sinscopefilms
body: Flow is one of the most visually stunning and innovative animations I've ever seen. The film's no dialogue only enhances its storytelling, perfectly embodying the "show, don't tell" principle. From the start, it grips you with its emotional depth and remarkable world-building. The production design is nothing short of tremendous, creating a rich, immersive world devastated by a great flood.The sound design plays a pivotal role, adding layers of realism to the film's events, making every moment feel visceral and alive. The film's ability to evoke deep emotion, especially for the animals, truly moved me - it had me in tears more than once. I also loved the use of shaky cinematography throughout the film, which gave the film an added sense of urgency and rawness.The original soundtrack is mysterious and perfectly suited to the film. It weaves tension, curiosity, and surprise into key moments, making the experience even more powerful. The cat, as the central character, carries the film effortlessly. The entire plot feels surreal, with the animals driven by survival instincts. Each animal's unique personality shines: the cat is naturally skeptical, the capybara serves as a gentle caretaker, the dog embodies a loyal golden retriever, the lemur is selfish and materialistic, and the bird feels like the cat's guardian angel.The film's core theme is fear, which is explored beautifully through visual storytelling. Even with no dialogue, there's palpable drama and tension throughout, proving that words aren't necessary to convey deep emotional weight. The film is visually provocative, and the way it communicates complex emotions is brilliant.The ending is wholesome and heartfelt, wrapping up a truly moving journey. I sincerely hope this film wins an Oscar, as it deeply touched me. Flow is a cinematic masterpiece, both emotionally and visually.

title: A Visual Treat, but...
author: barefootstallion
body: There is just no cohesive story. It is more like a painting brought to life, but one that leads the viewer into no conclusions. A treat for the eyes, but none for thought.Also, there is just enough anthropomorphism to detract from what the artists are apparently hoping to convey with the characters. Animals on a journey together, but that demonstrate a bit too much reasoning to be believed as just animals.But that, honestly, was the only things that detracted any from it for me. It was a stunning broad stroke of a world of beauty and depth. Delightful visuals abound throughout, and all of them done in lovely pastel artistry. The sound design was equally immersive. And the characters, while made somewhat difficult to relate to, were lovingly presented.If I were asked to compare it to any other artform, I would have to say it would be like going to an aquarium. Watch the lovely sea life through the glass, permit yourself to be carried away by your imagination a bit, and then it's time to get back to life.In all, it wasn't a let down or a disappointment, but I think it could have been a whole lot better if there was something that engaged you at a more visceral level, rather than just a visual one.

title: A Wordless Tale of Strength and Beauty
author: ddis
body: "Flow" is a one-of-a-kind, captivating film that packs a lot of meaning into every scene. The film's striking visuals and heartfelt moments create a deep connection with the audience, pulling them into a journey of survival and quiet determination. The film's pacing allows the story to unfold naturally, making each scene feel significant without forcing emotions. It's a refreshing experience that showcases resilience in a subtle yet impactful way. The minimalist approach allows viewers to project their own interpretations onto the unfolding events, making it a highly immersive and personal journey. Its combination of visual beauty and emotional depth leaves a lasting impression.

title: An International Sensation in the Making
author: chilebruv
body: All patriotism and Baltic pride aside, I think "Flow" may be the greatest animated film of the 21st century, and it will, without a doubt, go into Latvian cinematic history as one of the most exquisite, unique and courageous pictures of all time.As a prerequisite, I must say that on the surface "Flow" may seem like a children's movie, but as I'm sure all viewers would testify - it is not. I think part of the beauty of the film is its ability to speak to people of all ages and even more so - of all nationalities. Frankly, I thought the era of silent films was long gone, and it kind of is, as "Flow" isn't a silent film by definition, but as a movie that uses no words I think you could consider it as such, despite its use of sound effects and music as its main and only source of auditory immersion, which, in my opinion, only improves the experience as the movie doesn't allow itself to fall back on dialogue as a crutch, and instead focuses on creating an atmosphere both visually and acoustically aesthetic.Going into it, I was somewhat worried that a film with such specific parameters in an increasingly competitive world of cinema would come off as overly pretentious, but I can confidently say that Gints Zilbalodis avoided that common theme of "deep" movies becoming unbearable because they insist upon themselves too much.To summarize: "Flow" captures the essence of life itself, and the pure subjectiveness of it, as an everlasting picture so heavily reliant on personal interpretation and experience which means any viewer will consider it in their own respect and as an allegory for something of indivudal significance. It is a piece of art as powerful as can be, and all one can do, is congratulate the director and the entire team behind "Flow" for creating an everlasting cinematic masterpiece.

title: Masterpiece
author: MazeMadnessWriter
body: Truly incredible must see.The movie is a visual masterpiece. There is no dialogue but there doesn't need to be, instead Zilbalodis chooses to utilise facial expression, music and visuals to tell a story that on reflection gets deeper every time you think about it. On the surface this film is about a cat and an ensemble of animals that survive a catastrophic flood, but there are so many more layers under this. Themes of friendship, sacrifice and even mystery endure throughout the entire movie. This film should win every award going because it showcases something new and unique, and it deserves to be celebrated.

title: The hero's journey ft. a sweet little cat
author: creepsarehere
body: This movie is very somber and lovely, with some of the most deeply beautiful animation you'll see this year. It's fascinating how much the animation software Blender can do! I hardly believed it when it was credited at the end.The behavior of the animals is spot on, while being just anthropromorphized enough to tell a story. It touches deeply on the fear of change that I personally struggle with all the time, portrayed with an animal I relate to very much.This is the kind of stuff you can only get from film festivals - beautiful works of passion. Make sure you bring a box of tissues, but this is easily a must-see.

title: Beautiful graphics, fun, emotional movie
author: wkettler
body: I loved this much more than I expected to. It is a world that includes some magical mystery to say the least, none of which are really answered, but it adds to the film's magical qualities, especially considering the major players: a cat, a golden retriever, a capybara, a crane, and a whale/something else.This is not a film just for cat lovers. I am sick of cat pics and home cat videos on the internet. This is an excellent film that happens to feature a cat as it's main protagonist, as it transitions from a distrusting, fearful prey animal, to a participatory, group-leading friend and ally.Give this one a shot. It deserves it.

title: Black Cat Supremacy!
author: rhmylstr
body: The score I gave may be biased because I just really love cats. I even have one, exactly in black.I like how the animals' behavior is shown realistically, for example how a cat's eyes widen when they're interested in something, or how a friendly Labrador Retriever smiles happily. I like how they make sounds to give to the animals, I heard the film crew is really serious about that.In terms of story, it's actually quite simple. It doesn't require you to think too much about it. A movie suitable for children, but they will keep asking you questions throughout the film. LOL.The idea may be quite cliche, about how a group of different animals look after each other and care for each other, but I like it. And I love the visual. There's something magical about it.I definitely want to watch it again whenever I get the chance.

title: A Work of Art
author: daniel_d-08951
body: In a world where Pixar / Disney have an unlimited budget and focus on CG nonsense and garbage movies, you have Flow - a beautiful work of art. Without a word said, it takes you on an amazing adventure where a black cat has to make friends and learn to work together with strangers towards a common goal - survival. Visually and in terms of art style and sound, the movie reminds me of a few video games like Rain World, Far: Lone Sails and Stray. The focus was not on the most realistic lighting and materials or animations, but on the beautiful art style, camera movement, pacing, overall world and the emotions behind what the animals are doing. A very memorable movie and one of the best animated movies I've seen in a long time. I hope this team makes a lot more movies.

title: The perfect movie, that can unite multiple different people
author: emilijakitijabranta
body: The movie doesn't have any language barriers. It's interesting both to youth and older people. It's a sweet touching movie, which really mesmerises you. The whole movie was like a river. The plot is both peaceful and interesting at the same time. I love the wonderful world the director has created. Truly, a fantastic film.It tackles important problems. It shows how a crisis can unite different people and how relationships progress. It shows our basic instincts, the humane side of life. The digital design was fantastic! The shading was a bit unnatural, but it gave the whole movie a unique feel, making me admire every detail and movement. I've never seen anything like it.

title: AMAZING
author: johnny-89987
body: Oscar should show courage and award the best animation to this film. An animation that advances the story well without a single dialogue in human language and creates a new style in the world of animations. A story of survival in the form of lovely animals. Ladies and gentlemen, we are on the side of a masterpiece and an artistic achievement. The animation is far from the atmosphere of Hollywood and glamorous animations. Very simple but accurate and beautiful. I have nothing but admiration for this work. I think it deserves an Oscar for the best animation of the year if it is lucky. I know it took a lot for it to come out so well.

title: A Beautifully Introspective Dive into Creativity
author: daninostop
body: "Flow" is a captivating exploration of creativity, ambition, and the personal toll that both can take. The movie blends stunning visual storytelling with an emotional narrative, creating an immersive experience. Its pacing is deliberate, letting each moment breathe, and allowing the characters' inner struggles to unfold naturally.The performances are solid across the board, particularly the lead, who carries much of the film's emotional weight. The cinematography stands out, complementing the story's themes of artistic expression.Overall, "Flow" delivers on its promise of an introspective look at the costs of chasing perfection. It's not a film for everyone, but for those willing to engage with its deeper messages, it's a rewarding and thought-provoking experience.

title: Different
author: imti-45784
body: While the movie isn't a first hit for many, it's different for sure, that must be said. No storytelling verbally, but with sight.It's surely as if you're watching a gameplay of "Stray" the game, while it's no where near to similar in their stories and plots but it's just what it felt like to me.Let's say it's actually inspired by "what it might be like" for nature to survive through natural disasters, while highlighting every living being's attempt in overcoming the hurdles in way for its survival and helping others out along the way too.Anyway it also leaves a space in your head to analyze what some scenes are trying to portray and such.It's a movie worth watching once.

title: Superb film that is full of magic
author: donmurray29
body: Giving this an 8/10 ratingWatched this at London Film Festival in IMAX, and it is just as beautiful as 'The Wild Robot', and both must be seen in as largest format you can, which is IMAX, so I did good seeing it in this there. Simple story of survival, a bunch of animals travel on a boat in bid to stay alive in a world flooded.What you get is laughs, drama, great music and sound design that have to and do, convert the narrative from the view of animals, so you get no speech- well just animal noises. A very calm film, and you could sit down and just dream along with it, the visuals really make this film flow easily, as the film touches upon magic and fantasy and ends as such.But this film is made with such passion and love, just like 'The Wild Robot', and really is a must see film, and in IMAX if you can.

title: Absolutely gorgeous with wordless storytelling.
author: themissdeelovely
body:
Last week, I was absolutely stunned by an animated movie that owed more to watercolor painting than typical Pixar fare and I raved about what a travesty it would be for the film not to win the Oscar for Best Animated Feature in the upcoming awards season. That film? "The Wild Robot."
Though I've been a fan of traditional animation since before I could even speak, I've really struggled with most of the huge films that everyone else has been so enamored with since hand-drawn animation seemingly became an obsolete art. Much like I had before seeing "The Wild Robot," I approached "Straume"/ Flow" with skepticism. Surely I couldn't be even MORE impressed than I had a week ago!"Straume" has a similar feel to the style of the animation. The backgrounds/landscapes often had me dazzled at how realistic they looked, particularly the amazing light effects that flawlessly recreate lens flare and the way the sun glints off the surface of the water. Really, the only criticism I can mention is in the designs of the animals. While there are animation sequences so realistic that made me question to what extent motion capture was utilized (particularly in the dog), there is often the feeling that an element is missing in their final rendering. Against the backgrounds, the animals often seemed as though we're being treated to a pre-visualization draft of the film. The black cat in particular - particularly towards the film's end - stood out in bright contrast without darker tones found in the scenery. They often seem like mere shapes of animals, which isn't necessarily a flaw rather than a stylistic approach, but there are times that almost seem unfinished.The film's real acheivements are in its ability to tell a coherent story without a single line of dialogue in the entire piece. This actually improves the narrative, and when you reach the end, you realize there wasn't a moment you weren't entirely invested in what was happening onscreen. Not a single moment of the picture leaves you bored, and that's not an easy task to accomplish in a film with no dialogue. It's also to the filmmakers' credit that much of what we experience is entirely open to each viewer's interpretation. This film leaves you thinking about what you've seen well after the final frames and it's a great conversation piece to share with friends.But of all the surprises I found in this film, none was more astounding than the fact that within a week, I'd found another animated feature even more deserving of the Oscar. For the first time in ages, I'll be anticipating the animation category at the Oscars.

title: Beautifully rendered and realized
author: Agent10
body: I'm not hip to Latvian animation, so I was pleasantly surprised to see this at my city's local film festival. While many are already expecting it to make a run for an Oscar, I certainly hope it can.Much like another film that recently came out, The Wild Robot, the themes in this film are pretty essential to the viewing experience. To survive a bizarre and sudden flood, you have to work together with a variety of people to make it out alive. While the titular ball cat is the protagonist, he ultimately needs his strange group of friends to seek out the end of their journey. Unlike The Wild Robot, the film doesn't rely on talking animals, but you get a sense they all have a psychic connection to each other. Amidst the perils of their journey to a mysterious rock, they stick together and also show compassion to those in need.First of all, the animation is quite amazing. While it is 3D much like its contemporaries, it feels like an older style of animation due to the shading and lack of precise detail. I also found the world this movie was placed in quite amazing. With the recent success of the game Stray and other animal themed video games, it's fitting we have a glorious film display the intricacies of animal behavior in a heart warming and realistic manner. I also loved the mysterious back drop of this world, for it felt like I was traversing a mysterious gaming world on another planet. Catch this film if you can...it is well worth it.

title: Director is trying too hard
author: danielmanson
body: To be blunt the film had me engaged and very interested for the first hour, but unfortunately it descended to a bizarre and confusing mess.I enjoyed how the plot went in a different direction to the first and yet stayed similar, the dialogue and acting I thought was great and just overall it was interesting and left you wanting more. However, the more it went on it just became so messy and I feel as though the director was trying too hard to make the film "thought provoking" and quite "artsy".I won't do any spoilers, but the ending especially just made zero sense. I had to google what the ending even meant and most critics also don't seem to know either, which speaks volumes. It's honestly such a mess! You can make a film thought provoking and have metaphors for life etc peppered throughout, but you have to incorporate it with a decent plot. And unfortunately this does not. It's just trying too hard at the end of the day and it falls very very flat and confusing.In relation to the first movie, a few characters return throughout and there was definitely some scenes and dialogue that relate back to the first, which I really enjoyed.Annoyingly I just can't get past how poor the ending really is. Nothing is answered and I feel as though I've wasted my time here. Directors and writers really need to stop trying to overdo this need to make movies in depth, thought provoking. If you're gonna do it, do it right. And this gets it wrong on so many levels (get it!)5/10, because the first hour is really good. But the final half an hour completely ruins it!

title: PLEASE, stop doing sequels that destroy the predecessor
author: robertodovalefilho
body: The Platform 2 attempts to build on the unique premise of its predecessor, but ultimately falls short of its predecessor's impact. While the first film delivered a gripping exploration of class struggle and human morality within a dystopian setting, the sequel feels like a rehash rather than an expansion of the original concept.The sequel introduces new characters and rules, but they often lack the depth and development that made the original so compelling. The social commentary, which was sharp and thought-provoking in the first film, feels muddled and less impactful this time around. The pacing is uneven, with stretches that drag and moments that feel forced or contrived.Visually, the film retains some striking imagery, yet it fails to evoke the same visceral tension that kept audiences on edge previously. Ultimately, "The Platform 2" feels unnecessary, as it doesn't add meaningful insights or innovations to the story. While fans of the original may appreciate returning to this world, the sequel serves as a reminder of how powerful the first film was-highlighting just how much it left to be desired in its follow-up.

title: What the f is this?
author: asafirda
body: No sensible plot. No nothing. Just bunch of nonsense. Halfway into the movie I can't help but wondering what this movie is about. And after I finished the movie, I still can't figure out what this movie is about.As the person who likes The Platform 1/El Hoyo very much, this sequel is very disappointing.I understand that maybe the writer or the director want a more cinematic movie. But can't you make one with a real plot? Not like this one. Wtf is this.Do not waste your time watching this movie. Highly anticipated but also highly disappointing. I waited days to watch this and I'm on of the first 59 people who gave stars. I watched this the second it's released. But damn I'm so disappointed lol.

title: No answers, more questions
author: sanuful
body: I don't think this film is for the average movie enjoyers such as myself. Even though the first movie ending left a lot of questions unanswered, I liked it. This sequel is of no difference. IMO, first movie showed us the consequences of capitalism and this one shows that socialism is no better. But where is the story in this? Where are the answers to the "normal" questions the fans had? Nothing was revealed. I'm disappointed. May be a sociopolitical expert can interpret it better than me. But for me, I needed some closure or answers and none were offered.On a postive note, acting was good, nice plot to covey the intended message, not boring.

title: Who on earth greenlighted this script and what were they on?
author: saradisc
body: Apart from the production design, the cast, and some photography, this was unbelievably bad. They took themselves too seriously because of how well received the capitalism allegory was in the first one, and the second one is about WHAT?? Religion? Legislature? Community? Juntas? Revolutions?It's an unnecessarily convoluted mess of a script that goes nowhere, neither as a prequel nor as a standalone movie. It's so awful that I went ahead and shaved two stars from my rating of the first one.Cherry on the cake, a man dedicated to a science abandons his work because he's conflicted about something from that science that is high school basic knowledge. That wouldn't be written in a script even by a hallucinating language model.

title: Frustrating
author: eduaranguren17
body: Like most of the people, I really, really like the first one, in fact is in my personal "top" of all time movies.With this one, I recall this sort of maxim "When a story needs to be explained, it's because it was poorly told"...So, in my opinion, this was a pitiful and unnecessary sequel.Few films have left me feeling as frustrated as this one, I cherish my time with films and other kinds of art, but this experience fell short.My hype wasn't so high, and yet, the outcome was a disaster.At the end, I get so confused about the story... I don't really understand why the same people behind the first one, wanted to achieve with this...

title: It starts well, then totally loses it.
author: Sleepin_Dragon
body: Perempuán tries to survive the laws of the jungle, as the platform, the food source for all the inmates inside the prison continues to fall, the source of life for everyone.I had all but forgotten about the first film, but I remember enjoying it, my hopes were high. Twenty minutes in, I was wondering how on Earth the films score was so low, forty minutes in I was questioning why it was as high as 5.The first half an hour or so, I really enjoyed, the dynamic between Perempuán and Zamiatin was great, sadly it all fall apart after that, the whole story of politics and society just didn't work, it became a poor art house film, too showy, lacking wny content.The whole gravity thing, honestly by that point, I totally lost it, I didn't have a clue what was going on. The ending was a total let down.Good start, shocking after that.5/10.

title: Giant Plot Holes
author: brunocmonteiro
body: The first movie was great, an original idea well executed that is beyond a movie, is a psychological study of human behaviour. The second one holds the interesting premise, but, unfortunately, as most sequels do, it wasnt able to achieve the same results. Great and well known actors helps, but they cannot move away the feeling that writters/producers/director were just out for the money, pushing too hard to make a movie that was ordered and not artistically created. The main problem here are the giant plot holes that end up disrespecting the original work. Somethings are meant to be a unity, not a franchise.

title: What did I just watched? BORED
author: sposrs
body: The first part was brilliant and I couldn't wait for the second part. The second part is a huge disappointment. This movie doesn't hold attention at all. It is very boring and full of pointless scenes. I barely managed to watch it to the end. The plot of the film does not exist. They probably wanted to make a movie that has a deeper meaning, maybe it does, but it was done in such a bad way that it is unwatchable. Save yourself time and don't watch this big trash of a movie. First part is incomparably better and if you haven't watched it, watch it. Because of the first part, I waited months for the second part and now this complete disappointment. The movie should be rated with one star , but because of the first part, I gave two stars.

title: to anyone who didn't like it...
author: Fgtranime
body: The reason why too many people don't like this masterpiece of a movie is simply they think too much of it that they miss the point, this movie is brutal mockery to humanity itself that's it, the platform will never see peace no matter what happen, religion (the young guy with curly hair)? Nah you'll still see people die and suffer, law? (the blind guy) nah people will disobey leading to dead and suffering both when enforcing it and when they disobey it, Marxism? Nah too good be true, capitalism? Full on chaos.... the system of the blind guy for example is perfect, absolute foul proof, but people still find a way to make it look bad, or take advantage of, and eventually overthrow, so nothing ever good will happen in the platform, as long as there are humans in there. We are evil in nature either intentionally (the rebels) or unintentionally: the blind guy with his brutality, and the girl with her arm chopped trying to nurture a man which if everyone did lot of people die lot more than one sick man, also the protagonist starting a rebel that turned into cannibalism feast, and the fact she feel like the good one because she helped one kid? Lol we humans funny and dumb sometimes.

title: A Promising Start with a Disappointing Finish
author: sipproject
body: This could have been a very good movie. About three-quarters of the film was brilliant, filled with meaning and powerful metaphors, much like the first movie. The character arcs were compelling. However, the last part is absolute trash. While you could attempt to draw meaning from the chaotic final segment, the sad truth is that it feels like a forced attempt to meet certain Netflix requirements. This results in a disjointed and out-of-place segment that leads to an ending that ultimately goes nowhere.Still, I think it was worth watching, at least for the first half, especially if you are a fan of the first movie. The early brilliance somewhat makes it a worthwhile experience, even if it doesn't fully deliver in the end.

title: Another bad sequel. Surprised?
author: mikeestradapagan
body: This could only be good as a YouTube short film, not as a one-and-a-half-hour movie. This movie lacks all the things the sequels usually do. The plot is almost nonexistent; it just feels hollow. Each character has a story that can be summarized in three words or less in the whole movie. In general, it is a super boring movie, not even close to the first one. This is more like a crazy WWE in the hole.This also has a lot of incomplete mysteries and real holes in the story. It is not even fun to watch; it is just a bunch of people fighting in "the hole," making this as bad as it can get. In conclusion, I would not recommend this movie even for short entertainment; it is just not fun to watch.

title: How can a sequel to such a good movie be so bad!?
author: phil-sydney
body: Ok, so the first 15-25 minutes were ok, some good character development and whatnot I suppose, but then something happened to the storyline and the whole thing fell off a giant cliff. The movie suddenly went from cohesive dystopian sci-fi atmosphere building to some mindless or impossible to follow mishmash of violence and abstract artsy crap. A bunch of horrible, out of place characters were suddenly introduced and incoherent relationships between the lead character and various other characters began to be suggested, but you don't actually know when, how and if they took place or if it's all just hallucinations. Maybe there is some logic there, but it was too boring and chaotic to follow and decipher. Anywhere, this whole movie felt like a bad acid trip after the first 20 min or so. Definitely skip this one and avoid making bad associations with the first movie and which was a dystopian sci-fi masterpiece. Sad to say, but this is an instant franchise killer, possibly even worse than Matrix resurrections, if that's even possible.

title: A huge disappointment. I loved the first one.
author: Fella_shibby
body: After having enjoyed part 1, I was looking forward for this one but got hugely disappointed.Inspite of too many questions n almost no answers, the first was was really impressive n captivating.Expected some answers n a satisfying ending from part 2, but the makers didn't show anything new, in fact more questions are left unanswered, same things from part 1 are included, nothing new or thrilling stuff added in this one.The suspense, the dreadful atmosphere, the dark comic, etc which were there in part 1 is all missing in part 2.Mayb the makers are short of ideas of how to conclude the film.

title: "A Disappointing Sequel That Ruins the Legacy of the First Film"
author: taarekmusic
body: Oh, it was truly disappointing. For the first half, the writer seems to have a firm grasp on the story's direction, building tension and setting up an intriguing narrative. But as the film approaches its conclusion, everything falls apart. It's as if no thought or concept was put into how the story should end. The final act feels rushed, as though they were scrambling to wrap things up without any real care or coherence. The pacing becomes erratic, and the scenes feel disjointed, lacking the finesse of a well-crafted film.What's even more frustrating is the overuse of abstract and heavy-handed symbolism that is introduced without any context. These symbols feel like they were added for the sake of appearing "deep" or meaningful, but instead, they come across as pretentious and incomprehensible. Rather than enriching the narrative, they detract from it, leaving the audience confused and disconnected from the story. It feels as though the filmmaker was trying too hard to be avant-garde or unconventional, but it backfires, making the entire experience feel hollow and superficial.What's worse is that this sequel not only fails to live up to the expectations set by the first film but actively diminishes the original. It doesn't enhance or build upon the rich world and characters from the first movie-instead, it undermines everything that made it memorable. The charm, emotional depth, and the carefully woven narrative of the original are lost in a frantic attempt to make the sequel seem unique and edgy. Ultimately, it tarnishes the good memories fans had of the first film, turning what could have been a rewarding continuation into a disjointed and frustrating mess that leaves you feeling more disappointed the longer you reflect on it.

title: I liked it but not great as first one.
author: Horrorlover-97206
body: Netflix has a great horror movies besides another genres. This is one of them. The first one was actually great and I surprised but if the end was a little bit changed first movie would be perfect a movie. This one is also good but of course not as first one. But I say that do not be so prejudgement for this movie guys. It is definitely worth seeing. If you loved first one then you will like it. However, this is definitely not a trash. Acting is ok for me. Shots were really nice. I do not want to give any spoiler about the platform 2 I think it is definitely worth to see. I would give it 6 but since I loved first one I gave it 7. Have a nice watch.

title: An Extraordinary Film That Invites Interpretation and Mystery
author: DecybelAtom
body: I think the movie is really good, because the pure story, the pure movie is a matter of interpretation. Yes, I also had a lot of unanswered questions at the end, but through research I got deeper into the subject matter. Many people have written good interpretations and I think that's what it's all about. The movie is not like any other movie where everyone 100% understands what is happening. The movie leaves a lot of questions unanswered, which makes it even more mysterious than the pit already is. Some say it's a pure metaphor for society, others say it's a social experiment to study human behavior, etc.I recommend anyone out there who still has a lot of unanswered questions to simply do some research or engage their own brain.With so many movies on the market, it really is one of the most extraordinary and I think it's good that there is now a second part. Whether it's a prequel or a sequel (even here in the reviews people can't decide).

title: Worth watching through the credits
author: joshua-puig
body: Entertaining movie but falls short of the original. While the original is a slow methodical study in building tension, the sequel moves a little too fast. This movie poses an interesting study in comparison to the first. The idea that each individual selects their preferred meal adds a new dynamic to think about while rewatching the first film and is a key point focused on in the sequel.Interesting study as you are trying to figure out if you're cheering for the villain or cheering for an anti hero.If there is enough food for 333 floors, 666 (🤔) meals, what kind of person would you be if you went from floor 250 one month and up to floor 17 the next month? If the people above you ate your food and left you to resort to other methods what would you do?

title: Hmm...
author: fingazmc
body:
Bang average...
To be honest this should have been like Cube (1997) 1 and done (if anyone hasn't seen Cube and you liked the first one, go out of your way to find it, it's a brilliant film, TRUST ME! ).This one is a bit strange in all honesty, I know the original was as well, but there was reason behind the rhyme. Plus the Biblical and societal comparisons were open to interpretation, depending on how you saw it, which is a bit lost in this one.The first was a Seven or Eight out of Ten, but this one is bang, "middle of the road, right down the center Five out of Ten" average.Its worth seeing if you have seen the first one, but you won't enjoy it as much. It's a completely different style and type of film, but I suppose it's still worth watching if you want to see "A SEQUAL".....

title: Started out ok, but ends in a mess
author: wesperkins
body: The first half of the movie, I was actually kind of engaged with it and could tell what was going on. They had a decent plot compared to the first one. But it got really confusing and convoluted. I really don't even know what they were trying to say, and they were trying to be very artsy and cinematic. It's almost like this film tried to be too smart. Just because a film is different doesn't make it good, and boy was this different. The last twenty minutes of this, I had to I force myself to finish, just in case something happened. When you wanna turn off a film, it's not a good sign. I mean, I get that it is saying, no plan is going to work, or is without flaws, but it could have told it in a way that actually had a plot.

title: A surprisingly adequate sequel
author: qsraines
body: The title of this review is a hint to understanding the ending if you find it frustrating. If you liked the first movie, then watching this one is a no brainer. While the effects can be somewhat amateurish, the basis of the film is a valuable message. Regardless of what you believe, it is imperative that beliefs be challenged. The film explores how dogmatism and personal conviction are challenged in the face of opposition. If the first movies ending was frustrating or confusing, you may want to skip this one. The ending of this one is much more complex than the last. While I do not particularly enjoy the gore and violence required to accomplish sending the message, it is an extreme extrapolation that makes the message more obvious. The credits after the initial ending explain the full premise and ending of both films a bit more clearly. Several pages could be written about the ending of the film, but I will simply say that I love it.

title: Solid Sequel But Lacking Compared To The first
author: TharsheyN
body: The Platform 2 attempts to build upon the success of its predecessor, offering a similarly intriguing concept but falling short in its execution. The movie starts strong with an interesting expansion on the original's dystopian premise. Once again, we find ourselves in a towering vertical prison where a descending platform of food serves the inmates. However, this time, the story introduces new elements of law and order, aiming to bring a semblance of control to the chaos.However, where The Platform 2 falters is in its complexity. The story becomes confusing as it progresses, especially when it comes to the introduced law system. Initially, the idea of having rules and regulations to manage the prison seemed promising. But as the film continues, this legal system begins to feel more like a mechanism to oppress the prisoners rather than a tool for order. Instead of offering clarity, the rules feel arbitrary and designed to maintain the hierarchy and suffering of those inside, which detracts from the more philosophical elements the original explored though it also serves to show that different systems of law may work for a time before they don't.The film tries to juggle too many ideas at once, which muddles the core message. While the first film thrived on its simplicity and thought-provoking commentary on inequality and selfishness, the sequel's more convoluted plot loses focus. The increasing confusion makes it difficult for viewers to fully grasp the film's message, leaving some of its most important themes underdeveloped.The cast is solid, with Milena Smit playing the lead Perempuan and doing a stand out job in the role! We also have the beautiful Natalie Tena among others giving us lovely performances as the supporting cast. The character interactions reflect the harsh realities of their situation, highlighting their struggle to survive while dealing with morality and human nature.The VFX and SFX are amazing, no issue there with the design of the sets and the accompanying visuals and visual effects.Overall I give the movie a 6/10. The movie is interesting and the addition of laws is a nice plot point, especially as it is interpreted in its own way by each person. The cast is lovely with solid leads and the vfx and sfx are also a pleasure for the audience.

title: A Visually Striking but Less Impactful Follow-Up
author: ahmetcanerkara-62536
body:
The Platform 2 (2024), the highly anticipated sequel to the 2019 dystopian hit The Platform, attempts to expand on the original's unique social commentary while delivering more of the gruesome thrills that made the first film stand out. Directed by Galder Gaztelu-Urrutia, the sequel offers an engaging continuation, but it doesn't quite capture the sharpness or intensity of the original.Pros:
Striking Visuals: One of the strongest aspects of The Platform 2 is its visual style. The dark, gritty aesthetic of the platform prison returns, but this time with some new and inventive designs that give the sequel its own identity. The vertical prison still feels claustrophobic and unsettling, which adds to the tension and overall mood of the film.Expanding the World: The sequel dives deeper into the mechanics and history of the platform prison, shedding light on how it came to be and introducing new characters that add complexity to the system. For fans of the original, this expansion of the world is interesting and adds more layers to the film's dystopian setting.Social Commentary: Like the first film, The Platform 2 continues to explore themes of inequality, survival, and the consequences of a rigid class system. It touches on timely issues of wealth distribution, but it feels a bit more heavy-handed this time around, lacking the subtlety of the original.Solid Performances: The cast delivers strong performances, with returning characters and new faces alike bringing depth to their roles. The moral dilemmas and psychological strain that the characters face are portrayed convincingly, keeping the audience emotionally connected to the story.Cons:
Lacking Originality: While the film expands the platform's world, it doesn't bring much new to the table in terms of plot or concept. The structure and pacing follow a similar pattern to the first film, which can make it feel repetitive at times. Fans expecting a completely fresh take may feel slightly disappointed.Weaker Emotional Impact: One of the first film's strengths was its brutal, gut-wrenching portrayal of humanity's darker side. The Platform 2 tries to replicate that intensity but doesn't quite reach the same emotional depth. While the stakes are still high, the emotional punch isn't as strong this time around.Pacing Issues: The movie struggles with pacing in the middle section. While the build-up and final act are gripping, the story lags a bit as it tries to introduce new elements and characters. This makes the film feel longer than it is, dampening some of the tension.Conclusion:
The Platform 2 (2024) is a visually impressive and thematically rich sequel, but it doesn't fully recapture the raw impact of the original. While it expands on the universe and delivers more of the disturbing, dystopian atmosphere that fans loved, it lacks some of the originality and emotional resonance that made the first film stand out. It's a solid follow-up, but it falls short of the groundbreaking heights of its predecessor. 7/10.

title: A Strong Start, but Fades into Confusion
author: huseynsukurov
body: The Platform 2 starts off in a familiar setting with the same dark and intense vibe as the first movie. The idea of the vertical prison and the platform carrying food down to the prisoners is still interesting, but this time the story feels more confusing and hard to follow. The new characters, like Perempuan and the Loyalists, don't have clear motivations, and the movie struggles to make its message clear. It introduces religious and political themes, but they're not explained well, which makes the plot feel all over the place.Overall, it feels like the movie is just repeating what the first one did, without adding anything new. The original tension and clever commentary on society are mostly lost. While there are a few exciting moments, the sequel doesn't deliver the same impact and leaves the audience with more questions than answers.

title: Despite the other reviews - an alright film
author: hannahvachre
body: I really liked the first film and understand why there's a lot of people frustrated with the second. So, firstly and importantly be prepared that there are no answers to the first film.With that understanding you can enjoy the film for what it is.Yes it's a bit of a rehash of the first one, but if you enjoyed the first then...why not. There is a different set of characters and different spin on the first film which I enjoyed.A lot of people who have taken issue with the film appear to dislike that elements are (I think purposefully) left to the viewer's interpretation.
