The overall story is more than worth the time, so I'll give it a mild recommendation, but maybe temper your expectations, especially if you've been looking forward to this one. IF is a great story in a mediocre execution of a movie. It's now playing in theatres, but you can wait for this one.

title: Loved it
author: LinCar47
body:
We talked about it all the way home. We absolutely loved it, loved the girl, loved the plot twist, loved the characters and want to go again to watch for hints of what we missed
because we were so wrapped up in the story. This is a very real story inside of a fantasy and a poignant reminder of the importance of love and connection even when life is hard. Bad things happen and it hurts, but love and imagination and knowing you can find ways to cope is a lesson meta naysayers seem to have missedI cannot understand the low meta rating...is media just that jaded ? It is a beautiful story and so worth seeing.

title: hokey but ultimately very sweet
author: SnoopyStyle
body: 12 year old Bea (Cailey Fleming) returns to her childhood home after many years away. Her father (John Krasinski) tries to be playful, but she's not in the mood. Her grandmother (Fiona Shaw) is taking care of her. She encounters Cal (Ryan Reynolds) who introduces her to a world of IF (Imaginary Friends). These IF have been left behind after their children forgot about them.This is written and directed by John Krasinski. The story is rather hokey but ultimately very sweet. Cal becomes very obvious at the auditions. Those scenes is the confirmation of a long standing suspicion. The missing mom and father part is a bit more complicated. There is some logistic math being done. There are only a few possible solutions. In some ways, it would be more compelling to simply tell the family's story straight. As a matter of logic, this kid is off on her own a lot. There is being independent and then there is being abandoned. It felt weird that she's in the city by herself all the time. This is a movie with a sweet sincere idea, but a few more cycles through the rewrite machine would help.

title: I'm annoyed that it wasn't as good as it should have been
author: ta-60644
body: There was so much possibility here. It is a really cute premise with so much possibility.The problem is every character was really one dimensional.Krasinski was the quintessential "I'm the worlds best father ever!!!". It was to the point where he didn't seem human, so it was hard to connect with his character and his character's feelings.Reynolds was more subdued than I thought he could play, which fit at times but at other times I really missed his charm and humor.For Fleming, I realize it is hard to play an angsty pre-teen and remain likeable and then transition to a caring young person in a smooth manner. However I would have liked a bit more surprise and wonder at what was happening around her. She charged through too much of the parts that should have had her amazed as though she did that every day. If she wasn't in wonder of what was around her, then why should we be?They really didn't seem to explore the possibilities with the animated characters, their real feelings, personalities and abilities.Live actors interacting with what will be added later is an art form into itself and this lacked the connection between the worlds.At the start, the musical score seemed strong but as the movie went on it seemed like an over used laugh track. For everything that happened they built the music up like it was the peak moment in the movie. If the music is done right it flows with the moments, this one tried to use it to force the moments.The setup felt very long and there were a lot of slow parts throughout. And many of the slow parts didn't need to be. A bit more of Reynolds humor and of Fleming being in awe of what was going on would have gone a long way to drawing us into the movie.The closing credit moments were touching but that is a lot of movie to sit through to get to that.

title: IF
author: CinemaSerf
body: "Bea" (Cailey Fleming) arrives to stay with her grandmother (Fiona Shaw) so she can be near her father (John Krasinski) who is having cancer treatment at a nearby hospital. It's a fairly traumatic time for everyone, but it also becomes quite puzzling for the youngster when she encounters "Blosson", "Blue" (who's actually purple) and their handler "Cal" (Ryan Reynolds) living in the apartment upstairs. She quickly discovers what an "IF" is, and is introduced to loads of them, now adrift in a world where their original partners have grown up and forgotten them. "Cal" and his friends are trying to re-home these friendly and creative critters, and so "Bea" takes an hand helping out. Their first target for a new friend is the friendly "Benjamin". He's a patient in the same hospital as her dad, prone to breaking his bones and though outwardly cheery and good-natured, cuts a rather lonely sight in his room. As the story continues we begin to suspect that it's not just him that needs an "IF". Sure, it's derivative at times, but there's an engaging effort from the young Fleming and the sparing use of the colourful and well integrated visual effects along with some cheery scripting and a few amiable supporting characters that could easily inhabit any toy-box (I liked the bear and the tasting marshmallow) wired well. Also, Reynolds takes enough of a back seat not to impose his presence too firmly on the proceedings. It's an amiable story about family, loneliness and growing up that encourages folks to use and enjoy their imagination. I wasn't really expecting to, but I did quite enjoy this.

title: A story you have to believe to see
author: MB-reviewer185
body: I like John Krasinski both as an actor and as a director, so having him direct and write a family film about imaginary friends with a lot of well-known actors got my interest, and when it comes to this film, I was expecting this film to be enjoyable or at least nice to watch; after watching it, I can say that this is an enjoyable and imaginative family film that was nicely handled. The film called IF (2024) was nice to watch with its great performances, funny moments, nice looking 3D CG animation, nice looking cinematography, heartfelt moments, and creative but simple imaginary friend designs; I liked the premise to the film with it sounding like Foster's Home for Imaginary Friends (2004-2009) the animated show on Cartoon Network, and I thought director John Krasinski did a great job with putting that premise in a live-action setting with the great 3D CG animation that makes the imaginary friends look like they are there in a scene interacting off of the main two leads.The performances from the leads Bea and Cal, played by Cailey Fleming and Ryan Reynolds, were both well-done with Bea trying to grow up too fast and being able to see a lot of imaginary friends and Cal trying to help these imaginary friends with finding a kid to be friends with; Bea was believable enough as this kid dealing with the loss of her mother and her dad, played by John Krasinski, being in the hospital while learning about imaginary friends and lending a hand in finding new owners. Cal seems like a grumpy character of sorts who knows a lot about how the imaginary friends work and where they live, and he can be funny at times, along with him being a likable enough character like Bea; Bea and Cal worked well together when trying to find owners for the imaginary friends, and they build a nice friendship with each other. Lastly, all the imaginary friends were entertaining with them all having well-known actors voicing them, like Matt Damon, Emily Blunt, Bradley Cooper, Etc, along with Steve Carell as a main one named Blue who is a likable character trying to find his owner; each imaginary friend had a simple but creative design, and they looked good in the live-action setting with its nice-looking 3D CG animation.The 3D CG animation for the imaginary friends was particularly good with it having nice details and made them look good in live-action locations, with them also looking believable when interacting with the two lead characters; I like that there is no villain/antagonist in this film, because it does not need to have one, it is just an entertaining and funny film that also has effective emotional moments. At times, the film would feel like it was going all over the place, but it was not confusing, and I felt like there could have been more done with a premise like this, but they still did a respectable job with it; the film is imaginative with how the imaginary friends look, how Bea's imagination works, and how imaginary friends find friends or their old owners, along with their being quite a bit of creative things involving Bea using he imagination to change look of a certain thing.The film called IF (2024) was nice to watch with its great performances, funny moments, nice looking 3D CG animation, nice looking cinematography, heartfelt moments, and creative but simple imaginary friend designs; I liked the premise to the film, and I thought director John Krasinski did a great job with putting that premise in a live-action setting with the great 3D CG animation, along with some minor issues with the film. This is just an enjoyable an entertaining family film that plenty of people will like, because this film took an interesting premise and did something fun with it, so I will recommend giving this a watch, especially if you like John Krasinski as a director; sometimes all you want is a nice heartfelt film to watch, and this is one of those.

title: Heartfelt and cute film but felt short and thin in places.
author: cruise01
body: 3 out of 5 stars.If is a fair family film that has heart, cute, and has a story that can relate to children and adults. The plot is okay. About a child whos father is in the hospital. She meets a guy who helps imaginary friends characters that noone sees gets back to there original children who are adults now.The humor is okay and cute. The characters are fun. Ryan Reynolds is also good with the role as well as Cailey Fleming. The film does have a theme of never forget your dreams as a child. The music scote by Michael Giacchino is good. John Krasinski did great with his role. His script and direction felt little short handed with the substance of the story. It was lacking a central conflict besides a child growing up and overcoming loneliness. He did okay for a family film. It was not the best. But it was not bad.

title: A 41 yr old, 13 yr old, and 10 yr old see a movie
author: fjfzrs
body: I had only seen one trailer for this movie. But with it being a John Krasinski/Ryan Reynolds project, it was pretty easy to be convinced to see it. I took my two daughters, 13 and 10. I had a pretty good feeling that it would be good. This film most definitely exceeded my expectations.The movie hit a lot of emotions, but that's a good thing. I will say that if you don't want your kids exposed to emotions, then it might not be for your family. Though it's ok to feel, too. However, I can understand if parents with kids under 5 wouldn't want to take in this particular movie.I was honestly impressed with the ability of the story to hit so many emotions. All three of us (ages 10, 13, and 41) cried a few times. But we also laughed. This movie had heart, and you can't say that about a lot of movies. Both of my daughters asked if we can buy this movie when it comes out. With all the streaming/renting options, we hardly buy movies anymore. So that tells me how much they loved the movie. I guess that means this dad will be watching this movie again. And what a beautiful movie it is. Highly recommend.

title: IF only this was a good film!
author: will-13780
body: I was SO BORED the entire film. I see what they could've done with this movie, but they missed the point tremendously. It's not a comedy (because it's not funny), not a kid's movie (they'll lose interest), and not a family movie (bc it should've stayed on the shelf). It's just there.... it's a good idea with bad execution. Someone definitely wrote this under the influence of something. I'm honestly really surprised they spent money and time producing this film. Ryan's acting was atrocious and over the top (He was trying way too hard); the little girl was a snooze fest; and the "IFs" were just all around bad. I would not recommend spending the time or money going to see this movie. I'm sure the good reviews are lies from the writers and crew.

title: Beautiful, new story
author: kellyrbass
body: I took my kids (ages 9 and just-turned 3), and I completely underestimated how deep this movie is. I'm so happy there's something fresh, not a remake or reboot or-as much as I often love them, a Disney movie. The creativity and thoughtfulness behind this movie was magical and captivating to all three of us! My children were not only entertained but emotionally touched by this story. My 9 year old related to the girl feeling like she was too grown up for childhood games, and I loved him watching her realize what a gift her imagination is. My 3 year old didn't understand much of the tragedy the girl had experienced, but she did understand she had suffered sadness and needed the comfort of friends. I laughed, cried, and left with a full heart! My kids are already excited to see it again.

title: Better than expected
author: lord_orsum
body: It's not often that a film, especially an effects heavy Hollywood film, surprises me in a positive way.IF presents teenager Bea encountering a group of IFs (Imaginary Friends) who have been forgotten by their now grown up kids. This certainly evokes themes explored in Toy Story 3, but is sufficiently different to work.While there are no major surprises plot-wise in this film, it does deliver an unexpected amount of emotional weight. The backstory of the mother is mostly implied rather than shown, and the relationships are subtly portrayed rather than hammering us over the head.Ryan Reynolds is suitably charismatic, but subdued (in a good way). The voice acting it top notch. And Cailey Fleming in the lead role manages to carry the film convincingly.

title: Tries too hard to force emotions out of you.
author: MikeHunt1075
body: IFThis film about assigning imaginary friends like it's a match making service could've been something decent, but its execution falls flat of being anything but a soon forgotten film that Ryan Reynolds made while waiting for his next Deadpool film to go into production.This film has an idea of what it wants to portray but fails to build up any connection with any of the characters for the viewers to care any less about.Everything seems to try to set up some emotionally uplifting pay-off in the end, but the build up is so quick that it is eye-rolling that the film is "This person. Who? Jump over any character development to care about. Something. All smiles and uplifting music" pay-off = Huh?Whoever this films leading little lady is has a dad about to go under some sort of risky operation and stays with her grandmother. She doesn't have the expected sad, loner, left out, unhappy vibe. She stumbles upon Ryan Reynolds who is some sort of rjngleader of Imaginary Friends. She pushes her way into his life, and then is shown the place these IF things live.There's no reason to care about how Ryan Reynolds character is supposed to be grumpy now compared to how he once was, and that small plot becomes extremely predictable what the outcome will be, leaving no surprise when it does to anyone over 7 years old.This girl then just gets told to use her imagination and suddenly becomes God of the IFs world instantaneously, in a very unimpressive sequence of CGI cluster and a pointless musical number. Then back to the real world for some more snorefest interactions of almost seemingless pointless dialogue and it just leads up to a Labrynth knock-off ending.The film tries to ram feeling good and smiling during uplifting happy music, with no set up as to why you're supposed to feel anything at all? It's like some stupid TikTok brain saw a film that did it, and said "who cares why? Just have the music kick in and make hearts glow and rainbows shine while everyone smiles and make everyone tear jerk at the happiness of it" but, without any setup as to why we're supposed to care as an audience, it's just lazy writing, or some sort of social expirement to see if people are going to feel emotional and tear up just because of the soundtrack and a bunch of characters in slow motion looking up and flashing their pearly whites.The only thing this film made me feel was rolling my eyes at just how pathetic the build ups are to scenes where you're being forced to think everything's all magic and unicorn poop to fool the adolescent or people with IQs well below average.Seriously, I'm expecting Dead Pool 3 to have some line about how IF was a late April Fools joke or made just to see if audiences even pay attention to what they're watching anymore and if competent writings even required anymore?If you like CGI overkill characters, predictable outcomes, sloppy writing, forced emotional scenes only a child or moron would tear up for, and characters you won't invest a cent in, then this is the perfect movie for you. Otherwise, don't bother.

title: Sweet but sad with some odd moments
author: sharon-terry
body: Cute movie that pulls on your heartstrings (I cried like three times during it) but there were some parts that really bothered me:why was a 12-year-old allowed to run around Brooklyn and Manhattan essentially by herself? The lack of supervision by the grandmother was shockingBea's dad didn't seem like someone suffering from a heart ailment at all. Even at the end after his operation, when he was supposed to be in a dire situation, he wasn't even hooked up to a heart monitor!why didn't the lonely fat cat at the rest home get a happy ending?That said, it had some very sweet moments. The part with Louis the Bear on the Coney Island boardwalk killed me. It was really well done but so flippin' sad. Anyway, it's a nice movie but it could have used a few more funny moments to counteract the sadness.

title: A Whimsical Yet Weighty Exploration of Growing Up
author: cutie7
body: This was the most Pixar non-Pixar film I've seen in quite some time! "If," directed by and starring John Krasinski, presents a unique story about a young girl who, after a difficult experience, begins to see everyone's long-forgotten imaginary friends. It's an inventive concept that's handled with a mix of whimsy and serious, adult themes. Krasinski's involvement as director, writer, and actor clearly shows, signaling a deep personal connection to the project. Ryan Reynolds also stands out, bringing a layered performance that adds depth and a bit of humor to the film with his usual charisma.Despite its creative strengths, the film struggles a bit with balance. It attempts to weave together light-hearted elements with more substantial, heavier topics, and at times, this mix feels slightly uneven. However, "If" remains deeply heartwarming and comes across as a genuine exploration of the complexities of growing up. The performances by Krasinski and Reynolds are especially noteworthy, each bringing their own charm and emotional weight to the narrative. Although it's not without its flaws, "If" is a thoughtful, engaging film that strikes a chord with anyone familiar with the bittersweet process of moving on from childhood.

title: Wish I had an IF like BLUE...
author: shashank_1501
body: Directed by John Krasinski with Ryan Reynolds in cast and voice of Steve Carell, enough reasons already to watch this film.IF (Imaginary Friend) is a story of a young girl named Bea going through a difficult phase and one day comes to know that she can see all the imaginary friends who have been left behind as their real life friends aka Kids grow up. So she takes a challenging task to find these IF's their match with Ryan Reynolds by her side.Carell gives the voice for the character Blue that is super cute and epic funny. Cailey Fleming as Bea is great and looks like she's got a bright future ahead of her in acting. She overshadows the presence of Reynolds which is easily said than done. Hats-off!!!In a nutshell, this Krasinski's anime-drama is right kind of funny and equally emotional and is for all age groups to enjoy.

title: Simple yet solid and effective movie
author: core_memory_jay
body: C. S. Lewis once said: "Some day you will be old enough to start reading fairy tales again."It's a simple yet solid and effective movie. It focuses on the relationship between a father (or father figure) and his child, but from the child's POV. It briefly mentions a more conflictual relationship with one own parent figure; it didn't give too many hints about that, I hope they will in future sequels(?)It draws inspiration from Disney and Pixar films, both in terms of story and design, and reimagines those elements in a way that's equally engaging, rather than a lazy copy-paste.The charm of this movie is that it appeals to more than just children. In this aspect, it reminded me of some classic Disney and Pixar films, as well as those from DreamWorks.''Rise of the Guardians," "Monsters Inc.," "Winnie the Pooh," "Toy Story," "Inside Out," and now "IF" all share a similar DNA but offer their own twists.Lewis (voiced by Louis Gossett Jr.) struck me as a grown-up, reimagined version of Pooh from "Winnie the Pooh." This was a nice touch, likely a nod for those of us who grew up with that animated classic.The VFXs were my favorite part. They were very creative, at times making the film feel more like an animated movie than live action, which I'm sure will captivate kids and immerse them even more in the story and its characters.The movie blended its elements well, likely because the creators had a clear vision of their target audience and aimed to create something that would age gracefully.Another great thing about "IF" is that it would make an excellent musical. I hope they consider this possibility.Every time I see Ryan Reynolds acting alongside a child, it feels like he's interacting with his own kid. He's one of the few actors who seems to naturally connect with and work well with young actors, making their dynamic believable.Cailey Fleming also delivered an outstanding performance. She's definitely going places. Her acting was consistently impressive throughout the movie.The actors who voiced all the IFs did a fantastic job. I hope we get a couple of sequels and the chance to spend more time with the other IFs. On that note, my only real ''complaint'' is that we didn't spend enough time with them. I understand the movie couldn't be too long, but those characters deserved more screen time.Even so, they were developed well enough that I'm sure kids already have their favorite IF.P. S.My eyes did water during the ending.

title: 😢Sad..... So Sad 😢
author: DoNotComeToTheCinemaDepressed
body: Just Got Out of a Screening of IF.Such a Perfectly Calibrated Film Across All of the Aspects Of the Filmaking.🏠📜 The intro, Build & Plotline - The opening "Shows you" and doesn't "Tell You" of the Tragedy. And then the rest of the build of the film is so well put together in this Slowly unfolding manner, about the IFs, the Plotline with Bea and her Role with the IFs, and also the Plotline of Bea and the Tragedy that hit her and then another trial(with the father) that is shaky and unsure of the outcome. The Reveal of Cal and what he was all along. It's just so good.🎵 The Score - Again, another perfect calibration, Firstly, we have the Tone of the Score which exactly fits this particular film, and then Secondly we have the Use of the Score, Perfectly Placed When Needed and this Score NEVER outstays it's welcome.😢The Tone of the Film - There's this Underlying Tone of Sadness Steeped within that's present throughout the Entirety of this Film. That's the Main Contents of the Tone, With Fits and Starts and Glimmers of Happiness.💭 Imagination Segment - This was such a Great Segment, the Part when Bea Is told by the Bear to Use Her Imagination to Create Anything she wanted and Ryan Reynolds' character is constantly on the ropes 🤣😂 through the hallways and so on. It was Such an Excellent Segment.💃The Dance Segment with the Grandmother - Such a Beautiful Segment, knowing her Story, and her describing the lighting and dust particles Whilst dancing when she was a Child and seeing her relive that Moment and Reconnect with her IF was Great to See.🙋The Performances - Cailey Fleming who is Very Good Here, Ryan Reynolds, again Very Good, and then we have John Krasinski who certainly adds to the film.🎭The IF designs - I really liked Blossom 🌼 and her Voice, Blue was ok 💜, and I really liked many of the Designs, Sunny 🌞, Unicorn 🦄, Robot🤖, Bubble💦, Art Teacher 🎨, Spaceman🌌, Ice Water🚱, Magician Mouse 🐁. All these particular Designs Mentioned, I really liked them.💬 - The Speech that Bea Gives near the Very End in the Hospital. It was so Emotional. There were at least 2 people Sniffling in the Auditorium from what I could hear.Overall, The Emotional Core Within the Film was So Strong.

title: Fell Asleep in the Theater
author: kylethegenius
body: Let me start by saying that I do agree with a lot of the reviews which state that the ending was the best part, and it did evoke an emotional response from me. That being said, the middle part of the movie was soft spoken and boring. There was never any real antagonist in the story or major plot development. The same imaginary characters were recycled throughout the film and there was only one brief instance where the true imaginative power of our female protagonist is unlocked. I felt like they dwelled too much on grief. I Kill Giants and Who Framed Roger Rabbit are much better! Disappointed to say the least.

title: Not a kids movie
author: wnyybwwph
body: This movie is absolutely not the movie we expected to see after watching the IF trailers. It is long, boring and drawn out. There are a few exciting fun parts but they're random and don't last. This film is for big kids ... 12 and up. My 4 year old and 6 year old were asking to leave but we had stayed over half the movie so I couldn't get my money back at that point so we stayed.The end has a twist but kids won't get it, it's like one of those mind bender movies that an adult will want to go back and rewatch with a new perspective.I'm not happy that the trailers make this movie seem so fun and exciting. It looked like they were going to have an imaginary friend agency for people to meet an imaginary friend and we would see their adventures and craziness. I feel deceived.

title: Go see it!
author: jonathansink-39825
body: Absolutely loved this movie, and so did my family. If you are looking at these reviews asking if you should? The answer is yes!!!I just knew Ryan Renolds was in this movie and that was it. Only decided to go because the kids wanted to see the film. I'm so glad we did. Some really good cinematography and an excellent soundtrack. The movie was a smidge slow in a few spots but that didn't deter from just enjoying a wonderful movie. It has been years since I just relaxed and enjoyed a movie, this was not the case and I may go again. It sparks the imagination tells a touching story all while being fun and laid back.

title: You Need A Friend
author: boblipton
body: It's a tough time for Cailey Fleming No longer a little girl, not yet a woman, she lost her mother some time ago. Now her father, John Krasinski, is in the hospital for something to do with his heart, so she's staying with her grandmother, Fiona Shaw, at her apartment in Brooklyn Heights. Cailey goes to visit her father every day, and makes friends with Alan Kim, who keeps breaking bones in falls but remains cheerful. But there's a mystery in her building. It turns out to be Ryan Reynolds, a grumpy ex-magician who's working with discarded imaginary friends to find them new friends. Gradually he recruits her to help, and takes her to the retirement home for imaginary friends underneath the Wonder Wheel on Coney Island. But as she figures out how to help the imaginary friends, she continues to worry about her father.Krasinski directed from his own script. Between him and Ryan, they got a surprising assortment of talent to voice the imaginary friends, who range from a giant, purple blob to a glass of water with an ice cube. Although Krasinski is unwilling to make the adjudment in the end about whether the imaginary friends are real or figments of imagination, he does make the point they are an absolute necessity for lonely children everywhere. I think anyone who ever had an imaginary friend or, like me, aspired to be one, will enjoy this sweet little movie.

title: Awful movie, IMDB rating is not justified
author: nainaprakash-72044
body: This was an awful movie to me. The first hour should have been done in 5 mins. Awful fake situations and background music to create unnecessary and unjustified tension. The story has no diverse representation - it is a story about trauma, being unsupported and dissociation done very poorly.The ending goes well because of the character's life, the point of the story has no impact to the journey.It is trying to be very cute but it would have helped immensely if there were actually a point and a story. None of the emotion landed for me.So so awful it should be rated 0.7 not even 1. Two hours of my life and 25 dollars I'm never getting back.

title: Fun, friendly movie
author: mahaliapolk
body: IF is a fun and very family friendly movie. There was much more emotional depth than I had anticipated based on trailers I had seen. The visuals were fun and well done, it truly felt like being in the mind of a child just on the edge of being "too grown" for kiddy stuff. I love the lack of cynicism for the main character, it was nice to see a family friendly film that didn't have the main child character be so focused on "not being a kid". I had expected that to be the main storyline; a young girl discovering that you're never too old to have fun. Instead I was happy to find that the central message seemed to be; your belief in yourself is your greatest strength. A thoroughly enjoyable film.

title: Ok movie.
author: goochbollard
body: I Went to see this with my daughter today. It's an ok movie. The fact she kept asking me how long was left every 5 mins can give an indicator on the strength of the story line. I feel that the end saved this movie a little as during the middle it was a little boring and no great story to it. It Is emotional towards the end. Ryan Reynolds is maybe a little quieter than in other movies that he has appeared in. The movie is 100 mins long...it's not the worst that has come out lately I would say its passable on a rainy day to watch. I don't think it will become a classic by any means. Go see it with not so high expectations.

title: IF
author: Prismark10
body: IF stands for Imaginary Friends. Bea (Cailee Fleming) is twelve years old and has to grow up fast. Her mother died of cancer, now her dad (John Krasinski) is in hospital with heart issues.Bea has been sent to stay with her grandmother (Fiona Shaw) in her Brooklyn apartment.Bea has put away childish things, but on another floor lurks things. Imaginary Friends that children have now forgotten as they got older. Cal (Ryan Reynolds) is the caretaker who wants to rehome them.Eventually a reluctant Bea helps Cal to track down their former owners.There is a lot here that owes a debt to Pixar. Some of the creature designs reminded me of Monsters Inc. The basic story was a spin on Toy Story. The toys left behind when Andy grew up and left home.John Krasinski as writer and director struggles to keep the whole thing coherent. If these Imaginary Friends disappear forever if remain unclaimed. How is it they have existed for years as some of their previous owners are now very old.Still despite the flaws, I did like it. More importantly it prompted to ask my grown up son about his imaginary friends when he was little.

title: You already know the ending
author: anjaruhle
body: I really wanted to like this movie. The beginning was really intriguing and interesting and Finn Wittrock is a favorite of mine (loved watching him in American Horror Story). I honestly don't think this movie would be watchable without him.So it starts off interesting but quickly becomes predictable and boring. I could guess how every turn of the story would go, and I want to be surprised watching a new movie. It's a slow burn, too slow.The ending is, well, predictable as well. I don't think a serial killer would give someone this many chances. I would have loved seeing this play out more in the eyes of the serial killer. What's his drive? What's the story? The script isn't as psychological as many other movies out there, and it falls pretty flat. I was having high hopes. It's definitely watchable, at least for the fans of Finn Wittrock.

title: Nicely crafted minimalist thriller that elevates its simple premise with a pair of engaging leads and tight film making
author: IonicBreezeMachine
body: Iris (Kelsey Asbille) is a young woman mourning the death of her young son from an accidental fall on a family camping trip. Waking up early and without telling her husband, Iris makes her way to her son's memorial in the park intent on jumping off the same cliff only to be stopped by an engagement with a seemingly well-intentioned stranger named Richard (Finn Wittrock) who tells her his own experience of loss with his girlfriend Chloe causing the two of them to walk back to their cars together. However once there Richard reveals himself to be a serial killer and kidnaps Iris knocking her unconscious. Thanks to a Swiss Army knife Iris manages to make Richard crash the car and escape only to be informed by Richard he's injected her with a paralytic agent that will work its way through her system over the next 20 minutes rendering her completely immobile.Don't Move is the new Netflix thriller produced by Sam Raimi and directed by Adam Schindler and Brian Netto who are no strangers to working with Raimi having directed Grey Cloud Island (Minnesota) for Raimi's Quibi anthology series 50 States of Fright as well as collaborating on their own solo projects like Netto's Delivery: The Beast Within or Schindler's Intruders. The film was announced in 2022 with a script by Schindler's Intruders scribes T. J. Cimfel and David White with shooting commencing in 2023 with Netflix acquiring distribution rights the following year. Don't Move doesn't reinvent the wheel when it comes to this kind of "cat and mouse" thriller, but it utilizes the format effectively to generate palpable tension thanks to brisk efficient direction and an engaging heroine and villain.If I were to compare Don't Move to something, I'd probably say the best comparison is a serial killer version of the movie Red Eye from 2005. Much like how that film was built around the tension and chemistry generated between Rachel McAdams and Cillian Murphy, a similar effect is achieved between Asbille and Wittrock. Kelsey Asbille does well playing a grieving mother who feels trapped by the world following the death of her son and it's incorporated well into her struggle for survival that gives her an arc for being able to live again. On the opposite side we have Finn Wittrock (who I mainly know from season 4 of American Horror Story before I stopped watching) who is very good as the man calling himself "Richard" whose good looks and charismatic charm are nicely contrasted with the darker nature that reveals itself and creates a terrifying character who can bend and twist reality on the fly to meet his ends. In terms of mining a feature length ride from the central premise of character being paralyzed I'll admit I was more than a little skeptical as while it's a terrifying idea it's incredibly difficult to stretch to feature length especially when purposefully limited (such as 2007's Awake which went to some inexplicable areas in its usage of Anesthesia awareness). Despite the challenges inherent in working with such a concept, Cimfel and White's screenplay does well in creating high concept scenario's that inhabit just enough believability (implausible as it may be) that we get some very memorable sequences in which Iris needs to communicate other than words to get help as it's out of reach only inches away. I also have to applaud cinematographer Zach Kuperstein who manages to take his largely wooded setting and keeps it looking interesting especially as it relates to POV shots from Iris making you feel her helplessness and desperation.I liked Don't Move and felt it was a nicely done thrill ride perfect for either a Halloween viewing with friends or just by yourself. What it lacks in originality it more than makes up for in craft, acting, and follow through.

title: Not too bad
author: lousha-1
body: I didn't expect much from this movie, and in the end it was actually better than expected. That's not to say it was anything fantastic, but it killed a couple of hours (no pun intended...), and wasn't boring.The story took many liberties, so you really need to suspend disbelief and even your logical thinking, but in general, it was entertaining, if that's a word to be used for a film with this subject matter.The best thing about it was probably the acting. The two leads did a great job with the limited material they were given.All in all, it was worth watching. It will probably be forgotten in an hour, but at least it won't be remembered as a bad movie.

title: Entertaining psycho thriller
author: Luigi Di Pilla
body: It was better than I have expected and don't believe to all the negative reviews on IMDb.The wonderful landscapes combined with a psycho murder made together a real popcorn thriller. The main actors delivered good performances and the director Sam Riami created with his experience a dark Netflix movie with suspense. The story is simply but there many surprises and turns that it was never boring. The running time is not too long. The end I have seen coming far away but anyway it worked really for an entertaining Saturday evening.The actual rating here of 5.8 matches nearly with my vote of 6/10.

title: Awful
author: martinrobertson300482
body: Yet another limp effort from Netflix. The Gimmick of having the heroine of the movie unable to move for most of a films running time will have some giving this a watch. But its as unexciting as it sounds really.The main actress does fine, and i hope she goes on to do better things. But everyone else in the movie is so dumb. What is the kidnapper/killers plan half the time? Why is every potential rescuer so stupid and wastes so much time? And why does everybody want to sit around having a chat when there's stuff to deal with? Probably just so the whole thing can reach that hour and a half mark. As it rolls along to an unlikely ending.It all feels like a film nobody really wanted to put on a big screen, as it doesn't know what to do with the idea, has no suspence, and also has the standard cheap and unnecessary CGI we've all come to expect these days. Just have a lie down on the couch yourself and watch something else instead.

title: Fun, tense thriller
author: filmephile
body: I don't understand the low ratings. This certainly isn't an Oscar-winning masterpiece that will change your life, but just because it's not doesn't mean it's bad or mediocre, like some reviewers may have you believe. This is a solid cat-and-mouse thriller. It follows Iris, a grieving young mother who visits the makeshift memorial of her late son in the woods. There she meets Richard, who soon injects her with a paralytic agent, causing her body to freeze up and shut down within 20 minutes.The film manages to maintain a genuinely tense atmosphere throughout. There's a great deal of tension and suspense. The acting from the two central actors, Asbille and Wittrock, is really great. Moray Treadwell and Daniel Francis are also good. Treadwell's British accent does come and go, when he's seemingly supposed to be playing an American. Francis is convincing and good as the inquisitive, skeptical cop. The action scenes are realistic yet graphic. The film does a good job of including several close-call scenes throughout the film where Iris comes close to being rescued or escaping, only to be thwarted by Richard. That was really effective, and further elevated the unsettling ambience. This is reminiscent of another film that's somewhat similar, Alone (2020). If you enjoyed that, you'll enjoy this too.Really entertaining, tense, unsettling, and suspenseful. The premise is simple, but where this film shines is in its great execution. A fun watch.

title: Simple Plot...Edge Of Your Seat Thriller!
author: estjake
body: Don't Move is a new Netflix thriller that just dropped and it's one I'd highly recommend. It has a simple plot with nothing new or crazy but it's just a really solid heart pounding film that will keep you on the edge of your seat from beginning until the credits roll.Great casting for this movie. Kelsey Asbille (Iris) nails her role in this, she was great in Yellowstone and she's in another one of my favorite thrillers (Wind River) check it out if you haven't seen it. I knew Finn Wittrock (Richard) would be great in this from years of watching him in American Horror Story and he was.The main attraction to this movie for me, besides the trailer, was that Sam Raimi produced this film. I've always been a huge fan of his work. Great job on the cinematography in this film, it was beautifully done.Netflix has been putting out some very solid movies lately with Rebel Ridge, Woman of the Hour, and now this. Give this one a watch, you won't wanna look away once you start!

title: Pretty good
author: burkertduncan
body: I'm confused why people hate on this movie. It's not the best, definitely flawed but I swear it's so entertaining and NOT BAD!!!! This movie did what I needed it to do; entertain and make me nervous. I had a couple moments in this movie where my heart was racing and I TRULY cared for the protagonist throughout. This movie is not evil dead or hereditary status by any means but if you love horror or thriller movies this one you should see!The ending is not bad as well (contrary to what some say) definitely reccomend watching this especially since the runtime is extremely short! (1:32)(Still confused by the 5.8 rating this movie has right now)

title: Its like it was written by someone who hasn't interacted with other people before
author: jim6893
body: Don't Move (2024) is a horror-thriller that brings some standout performances and impressive special effects but falls short in some crucial areas. The film's atmosphere, enhanced by eerie visuals and realistic effects, sets the stage for a terrifying experience. The actors also contribute with commendable performances, immersing the audience as much as possible within the limited structure.However, the movie suffers from dialogue and character actions that often feel out of touch with reality, creating a barrier to full engagement. It's as though the script was written without a grounded understanding of human behavior and interaction, which becomes distracting as the story progresses. Moments that should be suspenseful or tense are undermined by implausible choices and stilted dialogue, leaving viewers questioning the motivations and reactions of key characters.The end result is a film with potential that ultimately feels disconnected, despite its visual strengths and competent cast. Fans of horror may appreciate the surface-level scares, but those looking for an immersive, logical storyline might feel let down.

title: Somewhat effective, but flawed.
author: Sleepin_Dragon
body: A grieving Iris climbs to the top of a mountain, with one thing on her mind, Richard follows her up, and does his best to stop her making a huge decision. Unfortunately Richard's motives for helping Iris aren't well intentioned.It's that film that everyone at work is talking about at the moment, and of course it's number one on Netflix.We've had don't breathe, now we have don't move, I wonder what's next, don't listen, don't look? There's definitely a pattern forming.It's a fairly effective thriller, albeit one that's fairly flawed. More plot holes than you can shake a stick at, and if you start asking how, why or what, you'll lose the plot, just enjoy it for what it is.Several moments of tension, a couple of thrills and spills, and it's fairly well acted.Lots of threads sadly just don't go anywhere, and unfortunately we don't learn much about Richard, his past, his motivations etc, but as a snapshot it's quite effective.An ending that made Halloween Kills seem almost realistic, he's one tough serial killer.6/10.

title: Fresh
author: vassiliskounelis
body: Don't Move brings a refreshing twist to a well-known horror formula, proving that familiar themes can still feel exciting when given the right touch. The film delivers non-stop tension, pulling viewers into a world where the terrifying concept of paralysis is explored in depth. This unsettling theme is central to the story, creating a claustrophobic atmosphere that leaves audiences feeling as trapped and vulnerable as the characters on screen.The way the story develops around this idea is truly gripping, playing on primal fears and giving rise to moments of pure, heart-pounding suspense. While certain elements of the plot may feel a bit predictable, the intensity and well-executed scares more than make up for it. The film manages to keep the viewer invested from beginning to end, blending strong visuals with a dark and eerie mood that elevates the horror experience.Don't Move offers an enjoyable horror journey that both frightens and fascinates, striking a great balance between classic tropes and innovative ideas. For fans of the genre, this is definitely a solid choice.

title: Unbelievably dumb
author: chrisholton86
body: I'm not often moved (no pun intended) to write a full review but felt the need to warn others. I saw the trailer and added it to my watch list then gave it a go - my advice is to not bother. Don't just put it on for something to watch as I fear this only encourages producers and studios to pump out more of this drivel.The basics premise for this isn't a terrible idea but the acting isn't what it should be, the plot is very predictable at every turn, there are plot holes and the cinematography is as dull and boring as the plot. It's so painfully predictable that you can guess the next thing camera pan/line of dialogue/plot 'twist'. Overall a frustrating and unenjoyable watch.Do yourself a favour and watch something else.

title: Deserves better than what it is listed
author: lillyhenson
body: It's a decent scary movie not like crazy good but good acting, good suspense. It's a fairly good movie I don't understand the 5/10. I would rate 5/10 on a bad movie that was slightly redeemable this movie is everything it tries too be.It doesn't try to be something big and grand movie. Just has about 6 characters who talk more than a few sentences It's a fairly small movie with a small cast. A 7 is justified for a decent movie with no large flaws and good story line.Also the main killer in this movie does not to be this attractive it's making me question things about myself. What in the world.

title: Creatively stretches a restricted concept into 90 solid minutes
author: jtindahouse
body: Is the art of a good opening scene starting to make a return? Probably not, but a couple of films I've seen recently have had good ones and 'Don't Move' was one of them. It's a tense little scene with a bit going on, but more than that it sets up the rest of the movie. It gets information across that will come into play later and sets the characters up nicely.My main concern when I read the synopsis for this film was whether they would be able to stretch it out over 90 minutes. The film uses some good creativity to stretch things out and keep the movie feeling fresh as things advance. It manages to make it work - just. I don't think they could've pulled off another 15-20 minutes and they were smart to keep the runtime at the length they did.This is a solid little thriller with some good moments along the way. It may not quite have had enough X-factor to stick with me for long, but there are certainly worse ways to spend 90 minutes. 7/10.

title: A Gripping Horror-Thriller with Intense Atmosphere
author: drlex-15751
body: "Don't Move" (2024), directed by Brian Netto and Adam Schindler, is a chilling horror-thriller that will keep you on the edge of your seat. The film follows Iris (Kelsey Asbille), a woman who, after a tragic loss, finds herself trapped by a psychopathic captor (Finn Wittrock). The captivity forces her to confront her deepest fears and desires, leading to a harrowing journey of survival.PlotIris, struggling with the aftermath of her son's death, is abducted by a mysterious figure who keeps her in a claustrophobic environment. The film explores themes of trauma, survival, and the human will to live. The captivity forces Iris to confront her deepest fears and desires, leading to a harrowing journey of survival.CharactersKelsey Asbille delivers a powerful performance as Iris, capturing the character's inner turmoil and determination. Finn Wittrock's portrayal of the psychopathic captor is chilling, adding a sense of unpredictability to the film. The supporting cast, including Dylan Beam, Skye Little Wing, and Daniel Francis, adds depth and variety to the story.Visuals and MusicThe film boasts impressive visuals, with a dark and claustrophobic atmosphere that enhances the tension. The cinematography, by Zach Cooperstein, and the score by Mark Korven and Michelle Osiris, create a haunting and immersive experience.Conclusion"Don't Move" (2024) is a gripping horror-thriller that will leave you breathless. The film's strong performances, intense atmosphere, and well-crafted story make it a must-see for fans of the genre.Rating: 8/10.

title: Solid 6 at best
author: jayarthurmackey
body: I feel like people gas every new movie on Netflix.. I won't lie, i didn't mind the plot but the execution was just not there. It seemed like the story was incomplete with a bunch of unanswered questions.. It's very predictable and not very creative as well as really slow.. i would have loved some kind of backstory or atleast a better story.. i would say a certain character saved this movie but it was only about 4-5 actors with little to no dialogue... the best part was the old man.. it seems like they had a plot and not so much an ending.. Not the worse but certainly not the best so give it a watch..

title: Don't Move: A Tense and Thrilling Ride
author: cobranj
body: Adam Schindler's "Don't Move" is a high-tension thriller that grips the viewer from its opening scene. The film follows a young woman who finds herself paralyzed after being injected with a mysterious substance. As the clock ticks down, she must outsmart her captor and fight for her survival.The film's greatest strength lies in its ability to create a palpable sense of dread and suspense. The minimalist setting, coupled with the protagonist's helpless state, heightens the tension. Every creak, every shadow, and every hushed whisper becomes a potential threat. The direction is tight and focused, with a keen eye for detail.The performances are equally impressive. The lead actress delivers a tour-de-force performance, conveying a wide range of emotions with subtle nuances. Her character's vulnerability and determination are both heartbreaking and inspiring. The antagonist, while relatively one-dimensional, is nonetheless chilling in his menace.While the film's premise is simple, it's the execution that truly sets it apart. The pacing is relentless, and the suspense is unrelenting. However, the film does falter slightly in its final act, with a few plot twists that feel a bit contrived.Despite this minor flaw, "Don't Move" is a thrilling and well-crafted thriller that is sure to keep you on the edge of your seat. It's a testament to the power of a strong premise and a talented cast and crew.

title: "Don't Move" is definitely worth seeing!
author: hitchs-990-193190
body: I recently watched "Don't Move," and it truly stands out with its refreshingly different narrative. Sam Raimi's involvement adds a unique touch, making the film engaging. Finn delivers an exceptional performance as a psycho, skillfully capturing the character's intensity and complexity. Kelsey also shines in her role, bringing authenticity to the story. Although there are a few slower moments that could have been tighter, the film overall is compelling. The ending on the boat ties everything together nicely, leaving a lasting impression. If you're looking for something fresh, "Don't Move" is definitely worth seeing!

title: Don't Move brings solid horror elements, good performances, and impressive effects.
author: kevin_robbins
body: Don't Move (2024) premiered on Netflix last night. The story follows a young woman with a troubled past who contemplates suicide by jumping off a remote cliff. Just as she's about to take the leap, a man happens upon her and gives her reason to rethink her actions. She decides to head home, only to encounter a local serial killer who injects her with a drug that leaves her paralyzed, unable to move or speak. After a series of events, she's left behind and must find a way to survive, all while the killer continues to hunt her.The film is co-directed by Brian Netto (Delivery: The Beast Within) and Adam Schindler (Intruders) and stars Finn Wittrock (American Horror Story), Kelsey Asbille (Yellowstone), Moray Treadwell (Pirates of the Caribbean), and Daniel Francis (Bridgerton).There's a lot to appreciate here. The opening cliff scene, followed by the story's sharp turn, is well executed. The fight sequences are intense, and the knife work-including the stab and slash effects-is impressive. The film also taps into the terror of being immobilized, which, though slightly overdone at points, is effectively portrayed. About two-thirds of the way through, however, the concept starts to lose some momentum. While there are clever twists and a satisfying ending, it ultimately felt a few steps shy of greatness.In conclusion, Don't Move brings solid horror elements, good performances, and impressive effects. I'd rate it a 6.5-7/10 and recommend seeing it once.

title: Good, but not great
author: daninostop
body: "Don't Move" left me wavering between a 6 or 7 rating, but ultimately, the quality of the acting nudged me to give it a 7. The cast delivers good performances that ground the film, bringing depth and believability to their roles, which adds a much-needed intensity to the otherwise familiar storyline. Each actor seems genuinely invested in their character's fear and vulnerability, which translates to a sense of realism that's often missing in horror and thriller. This commitment from the cast helps amplify suspense, even if the plot remains predictable.Visually, "Don't Move" does an excellent job creating a haunting, unsettling atmosphere. The set design is meticulously crafted, enhancing the feeling of confinement that the story demands. The cinematography takes advantage of these spaces well, using tight shots and darkened frames to bring viewers into the characters' headspace, capturing a sense of dread that permeates the setting.The continuous pressure of "time" amplifies the suspense and creates a constant sense of unsettlement, making each moment feel more urgent and perilous.The sound design and lighting work hand-in-hand to heighten the tension. The director skillfully builds suspense with subtle sound cues, creaks, and echoes, which enhance the film's scares. The movie uses silence effectively, creating an unsettling quiet that is only broken by sudden, jolting noises that land with more impact.Although "Don't Move" may not be innovative, it still manages to capture some classic horror thrills. In the end, it is a solid, atmospheric thriller that shines in its production quality and acting, offering enough suspense and chilling moments to make it worth a watch for genre fans.

title: Much better than I expected from the reviews
author: KHamblin-1
body: I found this thoroughly engaging from start to finish. Yes, it follows a formula but the performances by the two stars are excellent (especially Kelsey Asbille), the cinematography supports the plot wonderfully, the pacing is perfect, and the tension is gripping.There are no big surprises in the plot and the characters are not developed with any depth but that's not what this movie is. I appreciated that she was not a stupid woman and he was not over-the-top. The director did what he aimed to do, following the formula, and did it well. The theme of paralysis was a new angle and there were a couple of interesting twists like with the character of Bill (well-played by Moray Treadwell). And I appreciated the slight psychological aspect related to her arc. 90 minutes was the perfect length for this movie and there was no fluff included. Lean, interesting, tension with a new angle. Worth a watch if you like this genre. I hope to see her in more.

title: A good, clever, nonstop, but heavy thriller
author: alexanderliljefors
body:
Its always fun with new horrorfilms and new horrorplots getting onto Netflix and to the world of film! And its great that Netflix dares to try on these innovative films.Been looking forward to this since the trailer got it! It looked pretty good, but as many films, the trailer can be good but the movie really bad in the end, or the other way around.So i had pretty low expectations on this one, but i really felt like the plot was pretty interesting. Pretty unique aswell, as the main development of the story is to develop during only 20 minutes. Interesting to see how the film will use the rest of the time and how it will mix it during the plot.To start with, the filming and cinematography looks very good and smooth! Well directed!Much better then i thought, it manages early to give that eerie atmosphere and the feeling that your trapped and the horror that awaits and you cant escape
and it uses the time to create a non-stop thrilling and definitely not a easy experience.Pretty well acted aswell!A pretty clever film!A good, but heavy thriller that i really recommend! It's definitely watchable!

title: I did move,
author: ucelik-57131
body:
To get my remote and turn it off...I had this movie on my Netflix reminder. Read the reviews before watching and what can I say, the bad ones are the right ones...
What's with the high reviews??Did we watch the same movie?!I quit watching mid movie.I mean make it make sense: impossible.Conveniently written story, plot holes, weird acting, nonsense scenes... you name it, this movie has it.There is plenty of things that just don't add up and the movie fails to live up to its promise.Great potential and opportunity wasted into oblivion with this nonsense of a movie.Safe your time and watch something else...

title: Worth your NF sub and your time
author: Rjay-50059
body: Many reviewers seem to downgrade this film due to the lack of originality. Yes it's been done before but what's wrong with that? Do we not watch similar genres with the same kinds of characters, situations, and endings that we know and enjoy. Between the great acting of the two leads, the excellent direction, cinematography, editing etc., we end up with an entertaining, edge of your seat thriller that certainly kept my attention for the entire run time. Of course I knew how it would end but that was the fun part. Will it win an Academy Award? Of course not, but when I chose to watch Don't Move I wasn't expecting great art but rather an escape from reality for 90 minutes. Definitely worth the time and money.

title: I actually enjoyed it.
author: danielleshaffi
body: I really wanted to hate this one because it's just so over done but I don't think there was much wrong with this movie. It wasn't too much but it didn't give too little either.. I thought the storyline itself was just right.I was under the impression that the entire movie would be her trying to survive while her body shut down but that's not the case.It was entertaining enough for me to actually want to know what happens at the end but it wasn't ridiculous enough for me to give up watching it.It definitely was an easy watch though. Of course I knew roughly how it would end and yet I sat through the whole thing, just to find out if I was right. Its very likely I would watch it again in a few years to see if I have the same opinion of it.I'll be honest I only actually watched it because Finn Wittrock was in it and he never disappoints when it comes to his performances. He never does anything in half measurements. All that emotion that pours from his body when he acts is enough to save any terrible movie.

title: Don't Breathe, Don't Move! What's next?
author: funnycommentor
body: First of all, when I first watched the official trailer of the movie I liked it and I had high expectations about it. Eventually, it was as good as I had imagined and I enjoyed it, a lot. The movie synopsis was very interesting and mysterious, but it wasn't innovative because there are many movies similar to this one. The storyline was very well-written and well-explained, even though it was simple and easy to understand. The main character (Iris) was very interesting, well-developed and likeable. The filming location of the movie was only one, into the woods. The casting choices were nice and their performances were great. I have to admit, it was a very intense movie, action-filled and there were some nice chase scenes. It wasn't scary, at all and there weren't any jumpscares. Regarding the killcount of the movie, there weren't many death scenes, however the kills were very bloody and some of them were kinda brutal. Also, the cinematography was very well done and the musical score was great. The opening scene was predictable and promising, but it was slow paced. Gladly, the 2nd and 3rd act were both adventurous and shocking. The ending scene was predictable, but I still enjoyed it, a lot. Overall, "Don't Move" was a great survival/thriller film, very intense and I would definitely recommend it to anyone!

title: Surprisingly decent
author: grlym-46849
body:
Netflix is not known for many good movies ...or at least ones that are new. Usually they just show you good movies from 30 years ago that you already watched to death, foreign dubbed films they pass off as new and student quality films.But this one shocked me. With such a thin premise, it actually had some bite to it all the way to the end. I'm not going to say it was phenomenal, but it was a good watch. And by thriller and horror standards it held it own.Acting was good
Plot was believable
Filming was good
Twists and turns were well fed and not too much or too little.It left enough for the audience to fill in your own fears to make the full impact rather than spilling it out with cheap dialogue.

title: What?!
author: yelizva-890-805098
body: What is actually going on? I am really confused since there are multiple plot holes into the story. I genuinely thought I was going to watch something original for the first time after a veeeerrrryyyy long time but nope! This film is another disappointment with great potential. I highly recommend people to watch it and see how the story evolves in 90 minutes. At one point, I was convinced that they were taking the piss! Especially the last scene where the climax takes place. I don't mean to be too harsh as the topic is good but there are multiple questions that are hanging in the air and I am devastated 💔

title: "DON'T MOVE" REVIEW
author: Mr-Topshotta
body: Directed by Brian Netto and Adam Schindler. A runtime of one hour and thirty-two minutes. Streaming on Netflix with an R rating."Iris," played by Kelsey Asbille, and her husband just experienced a grave loss. Feeling internally conflicted and looking for clarity, "Iris" visited a site with a monumental meaning to her.While there, she encounters "Richard," played by Finn Wittrock. He looked harmless and seemed to come off like a genuine good guy. Boy was she wrong.This unsuspecting stranger is a killer who injects "Iris" with a substance that will make her easier to handle. In about fifteen to twenty minutes, she will gradually lose her motor functions, and the rest of her body will shut down."Iris" will be awake but completely paralyzed from head to toe. She will have to figure out a way to get away from this psychopath with a weekend murder kink before it's too late.Even when coming in contact with other people like "Bill," played by Moray Treadwell, or "Dontrell," played by Daniel Francis. A police officer. It becomes extremely hard to let anyone know you're in danger when you can talk and you're with a guy with the gift of gab. Find out how this all ends in this wild thriller."Don't Move" started great. I had a little apprehension about how the film would be. Even though it's barely an hour and a half long. The concept seemed cool and unique, but I had no clue how it was sustainable. Once the short time runs out, that should be a wrap. But it was done well.The beginning sets up plot points that will be used further down the line in the film. This was the second film I saw recently with a truly messed up beginning.As the film progressed, I was glued to the screen. I was into all the ups and downs. As every new character entered the fold, I got more curious about how it would play out.I enjoyed this film until the end. The writing started to take a dip. Then it got outright ridiculous. The horse came out of the gate strong, but toward the end, it ran out of gas. I hate it when films do that. It still provided a fun race before it tailed off. Because of that, I give this film four mor fires 🔥🔥🔥🔥.#DontMove.

title: Well Done Thriller
author: tkdlifemagazine
body: Don't Move is a well done thriller in the vain of Alfred Hitchcock films. The story is simple, but amazingly well executed. It is a small cast of very good actors. Finn Wittrock has played the villain before and he is good at it. Kelsey Asbile stars in the main role. I have never seen her before, but she is really compelling here. The reason this has a Hitchcock feel is that there are times you know what is going to happen but the strength is in the Direction and the execution of the story that makes it watchable. There is a trend, probably because of budget, the make smaller films, with smaller casts, that are story's sting,a nd Direction driven. I like it al lot.

title: Emotionless
author: k-43764-45779
body:
An overwhelming lack of emotion seizes you within the first minutes.The main actress is so cold, indifferent and insensitive that your first thoughts would be : "was she in fact already paralized by the poison?"
Her acting is so 'rigid', her facial expressions seem to be frozen and careless, and the viewers never get the slightest chance to empathize with her grief.Hence, you feel completely unbothered by the following ordeals that she might find herself into, because you didn't CONNECT with her story.I think there has been a terrible miscast regarding that actress, she acts and speaks like a robot; she is incapable of conveying heartfelt, deep feelings or emotions.

title: Definitely better than expected.
author: angotti81
body: This was a surprise! I threw it on with little hope I'd actually watch it while doing household chores. Both the leads really helped draw me in and the actors did a great job. It does follow typical tropes, but is creative enough to stand out. I think the guy from American Horror Story is well cast as the serial killer. Definitely fits the role well. I do wish they had fleshed out his family relation a bit more.The actress is great and also had a side plot that could have been explored more. But at the end of the day the script was tight, the action believable, and it was a fun watch. If you go in with low expectations you're in for a good popcorn movie.

title: Typical Lazy Netflix Thriller
author: gzgwmrq
body: The characters make the dumbest decisions and everything is beyond dragged out to make this a movie. This movie just feels like a typical Netflix low budget thriller. Throw two relatively known actors in a movie with not many people and nobodies and hope people keep watching because the decisions anger people to keep watching and before you know it the 90 minutes are up. This feels more like "content" than an actual movie. The logic behind everything in this movie just doesn't really make much sense and you would question anything beyond surface level you wonder if Netflix has a chat GPT model writing scripts now. The actors themselves aren't bad but the movie itself is just...dumb.

title: Good one
author: majo-trusik
body: I'm genuinely surprised by the low ratings for this movie because it's quite enjoyable. The cinematography is solid and visually engaging, making the scenes feel alive. Yes, the ending is a bit predictable, but it doesn't detract much-in fact, a different ending could have worked too. The main characters are really well cast, with the acting overall done well, bringing depth to the story. The storyline is reasonable and flows naturally. Sure, there are plenty of movies with similar themes, but that doesn't take away from this one's quality. It's entertaining and definitely worth a watch.I recommend it to anyone who likes slower paced survival/psychological thrillers.

title: Simple. Yet not half bad
author: danielmanson
body: Actually pleasantly surprised by this movie overall. Yeah, sure it's not going to blow you away, but it's a decent little thriller, with good acting and keeps you interested throughout.I was impressed with how it managed to keep the intensity throughout. Knowing it's on a women, who's been drugged to be paralysed, you half expect some slow scenes. But, the plot plods along very nicely and keeps you very much invested in what happens next.I would have liked a little more in the plot, maybe some sort of twist in the tale? Although it's a good plot and keeps you invested, it doesn't have that "wow" factor. As said in the title, it's very simple.The acting from both was fantastic I thought and although there wasn't a lot to go off, character wise, they pulled it off exceptionally. Again, a little more depth would have been nice and if fleshed out a little more the actors could have worked with so much more and I have no doubt they would have killed it.But, overall I enjoyed this movie and although simple, I find it's very effective and for a Saturday night film I had a good time with it. 6.8/10. (7 for IMDb)

title: A good film, that makes it hard to move off your seat
author: mrdanielkanewilliams
body: At the beginning Iris (Kelsey Asbille) goes out to a remote cliff face to commit suicide. Unfortunately, along the way she bumps into Andrew (Finn Wittrock) who kidnaps her. Luckily for Iris, Andrew doesn't check Iris' pockets and she manages to cut herself free with her swiss army knife. This then leads to a good fight scene in which Iris thinks she has escaped but she soon finds out that Andrew injected her with a muscle relaxant and as soon as that kicks in she only has 20 minutes to find help and/or a good hiding place before her body shuts down.Whilst Andrew tries to catch his prey he makes a few more mistakes and has some bad luck. These unlucky errors make him look sloppy and are a bit laughable which makes the film less intense but some of them do lead to a couple of gory fight scenes.I also like Kelsey Asbille's acting in this because she was very convincing when her body started to shut down and then very convincing again when she started to slowly get her strength back.I've read that some other people think this film should have been a bit longer to give the characters a bit of background. But I like the length of this film, because it just gets straight to the main plot and doesn't have a slow beginning.So overall I enjoyed this unique thriller and I might watch it again in a year or two but I'm not desperate to watch it again, so for now I would rather wait and see if it stays on Netflix instead of buying it on DVD.

title: Not amazing but not bad either
author: rebeccarforward
body: Compared to other Netflix thrillers out there, this is definitely one of the better ones. Great performances by both main actors and some edge of your seat moments. The dialogue is pretty good too. Sometimes with these low-budget Netflix movies, the dialogue of the main characters are eye-roll worthy, but not in the case. It's a simple plot with some holes and predictability, but I was hooked until the end regardless. Trigger warning (and very mild spoiler warning), there is mention of child death (happened off screen, before the events of the movie) which makes some scenes feel very heavy and emotional. But overall, I'd give this a 7/10 and say it's definitely worth a watch.

title: Just boring from beginning to end.
author: jacobniccoli
body: This movie provided no depth to the characters and left a lot of questions unanswered. For a movie like this to be good you have to somewhat feel for the character and what they are going through but you don't get that with this movie. It's just here's this person and here's this person, now watch for 90 minutes her struggling and him struggling to kill her. Went on and never really developed a thought out story that left you with anything. Would not recommend to even giving it a try it will be a waste of time. Might be the most boring awful film I've seen of 2024. You just didn't feel engaged throughout the movie, just left you sitting there wondering why most of the time, just bad. They also have to have paid a lot of money to be out as the #1 movie on Netflix because there is no way. I did like the you don't own me at the end though. Good song! Also I've never done a review before but this was that bad I had too.

title: Reminded me of Curve - Fun and Heartpounding
author: briandouglasnv
body: This was a nerve-wracking ride that grips you from start to finish, reminiscent of Ian Softley's Curve (2015) in its tense atmosphere and character-driven storytelling. This 2024 release is masterfully crafted, with every scene seemingly designed to keep your heart pounding and your eyes glued to the screen.What stands out the most in Don't Move is its relentless pacing and tight, claustrophobic feel. The film does an exceptional job of trapping the audience in a web of suspense, where every movement counts and every decision could be deadly. The cinematography amplifies this intensity, skillfully using shadows and close-ups to create a sense of entrapment, leaving viewers with a palpable feeling of dread.The performances here are top-notch. The cast brings authenticity to their roles, adding layers of realism that deepen the viewer's investment in their survival. You can sense the terror in each character's expressions and body language, a testament to the actors' skill and commitment to the high-stakes premise.Like Curve, Don't Move combines psychological tension with physical endurance, making it a compelling watch for anyone who enjoys thrillers that push their characters to the edge. It's a film that demands your attention, rewarding you with a suspenseful and satisfying experience.Overall, Don't Move is an excellent addition to Netflix's thriller lineup, delivering well-executed suspense and high-stakes drama. If you're a fan of survival thrillers, this one is well worth the watch.
